definition_zh: 微生物；肉眼不可见、需借助显微镜观察的生物
definition_en: a living thing so small that it can be seen only with a microscope
core_image: 一滴池塘水里挤满肉眼看不见的小生命，放大后显出球状、杆状与螺旋状的轮廓
scene: 这里指「微生物」。 A single microorganism in the pond water can start a whole bloom once nutrients rise.
sceneCN: 这里 microorganism 是「微生物」（第 1 个义项：需用显微镜观察的微小生物）；句意：养分升高后，池塘水里的一个微生物就能引发整片水华。图中可辨识物件：水滴、显微镜视野、成片变绿的水面。

pos.zh: 微生物（可数名词，复数 microorganisms；涵盖细菌、古菌、原生生物、真菌等微小生物）

微生物的

senses.title: A Microscopic Living Thing
senses.titleCN: 微生物：小到需显微镜才可见
senses.definition: a living thing too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye
senses.definitionCN: 小到肉眼无法清楚看见的生物
senses.example: Each drop of pond water holds thousands of microorganisms.
senses.exampleCN: 每一滴池塘水里都含有成千上万个微生物。
senses.why: The word joins micro-, 'small', to organism, 'living body'. The defining picture is not a particular shape but a scale: the creature is below the resolving power of the eye.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「小」的 micro- 与表示「生物体」的 organism 合成；它的核心画面不是某个特定形状，而是尺度：小到超出眼睛的分辨能力。

senses.title: A Unicellular Form
senses.titleCN: 单细胞形态：一个细胞就是一个个体
senses.definition: a organism consisting of a single cell
senses.definitionCN: 由一个细胞构成的生物
senses.example: A microorganism such as an amoeba lives as one cell.
senses.exampleCN: 像变形虫这样的微生物以一个细胞的形式生活。
senses.why: Most microorganisms are unicellular: one cell performs every function of life. The sense marks body plan rather than size, though the two usually coincide.
senses.whyCN: 大多数微生物是单细胞的：一个细胞承担全部生命功能；这个义项标出的是身体构造，而不是大小，尽管两者通常同时成立。

senses.title: A Broad Taxonomic Cover
senses.titleCN: 分类上的宽泛覆盖：不止细菌
senses.definition: the loose group covering bacteria, archaea, protists and fungi, and sometimes viruses
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖细菌、古菌、原生生物与真菌，有时也包括病毒的宽泛类别
senses.example: The term microorganism covers both bacteria and single-celled fungi.
senses.exampleCN: 「微生物」这一术语既涵盖细菌，也包括单细胞真菌。
senses.why: Microorganism is not a taxonomic rank; it is a convenience class defined by size. That is why it can hold several unrelated kingdoms, and why virologists debate whether viruses belong.
senses.whyCN: microorganism 不是分类层级，而是按大小划分的方便类别；因此它能容纳几个互不相关的界，也因此病毒学家会争论病毒是否算在内。

senses.title: A Soil Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 土壤微生物：地下循环的工人
senses.definition: a microorganism living in soil and driving its nutrient cycles
senses.definitionCN: 生活在土壤中并驱动土壤养分循环的微生物
senses.example: A soil microorganism released phosphorus from the dead leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一种土壤微生物从枯叶中释放出磷。
senses.why: In soil the word usually names a decomposer or a symbiont. The scale sense recedes and the ecological job comes forward: the organism is defined by what it does in the ground.
senses.whyCN: 在土壤语境中，这个词通常指分解者或共生者；尺度义退后，生态职能走上前，生物体靠它在地里所做的事来定义。

senses.title: A Marine Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 海洋微生物：水体中的微小生产者
senses.definition: a microorganism living in seawater, often a primary producer
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海水中、常为初级生产者的微生物
senses.example: Marine microorganisms produce a large share of the oxygen we breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋微生物产生了我们呼吸的氧气中的很大一部分。
senses.why: In the sea, microscopic algae and bacteria carry out photosynthesis and form the base of the food web. The word then points to a functional layer of the ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: 在海洋中，微小藻类与细菌进行光合作用，构成食物网的基础；此时这个词指向生态系统中的一个功能层。

senses.title: A Pathogenic Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 病原微生物：引起疾病的那一类
senses.definition: a microorganism that causes disease in a host
senses.definitionCN: 能在宿主中引起疾病的微生物
senses.example: The outbreak was traced to a pathogenic microorganism in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 疫情被追溯至水中的一种病原微生物。
senses.why: Here the neutral scale word takes on the medical role. The sense is narrower than S1 because only some microorganisms cause disease, and the speaker is naming that subset.
senses.whyCN: 这里中性的尺度词带上了医学角色；该义项比第 1 个义项窄，因为只有部分微生物致病，说话人指的是这个子集。

senses.title: A Useful Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 有益微生物：发酵与生产中的帮手
senses.definition: a microorganism used for fermentation or industrial production
senses.definitionCN: 用于发酵或工业生产的微生物
senses.example: A beneficial microorganism turns milk into yoghurt overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一种有益微生物一夜之间把牛奶变成酸奶。
senses.why: Humans have long used microorganisms as tools. The sense shifts from 'what it is' to 'what it is good for', and it explains the everyday phrase beneficial microorganism.
senses.whyCN: 人类早已把微生物当作工具；这个义项从「它是什么」转向「它有什么用」，也解释了「有益微生物」这一日常说法。

senses.title: An Indicator Microorganism
senses.titleCN: 指示微生物：用来判断水质或卫生
senses.definition: a microorganism whose presence signals contamination or a condition
senses.definitionCN: 其存在能提示污染或某种状况的微生物
senses.example: The lab counts an indicator microorganism to judge water safety.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室计数一种指示微生物来判断水的安全性。
senses.why: Public health cannot test every pathogen, so it watches a proxy. The indicator is chosen because it is easy to detect and travels the same way as the dangerous ones.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生无法检测每一种病原，于是监测一个替身；被选作指示者的微生物易于检出，且与危险病原走同一条传播路径。

intro.en: Microorganism is a nineteenth-century compound of two Greek-derived elements: micro-, 'small', and organism, 'living body'. The word dates from the great expansion of microscopy and germ theory.
intro.cn: microorganism 是十九世纪由两个希腊来源成分构成的复合词：micro-「小」与 organism「生物体」。它诞生于显微镜技术与病菌学说大发展的年代。

items.en: Greek mikros, the Attic form of smikros, meant 'small, little, petty'. Its Latinized combining form micro- became the standard prefix for 'small' in scientific English. Beekes considers the Greek word possibly Pre-Greek, so its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 mikros（阿提卡方言形式 smikros）意为「小的、微小的」；其拉丁化组合形式 micro- 成为科学英语中表示「小」的标准前缀。Beekes 认为这个希腊词可能来自前希腊语底层，因此其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Organism is recorded from the 1660s for 'organic structure'; the sense 'living animal or plant' appears by 1825, translating German Organismus. It rests on Greek organon 'tool, instrument', literally 'that with which one works'.
items.cn: organism 于十七世纪六十年代记录为「有机结构」，到 1825 年才出现「活的动物或植物」这一义项，译自德语 Organismus。其基础是希腊语 organon「工具、器具」，字面意为「用来工作的东西」。

items.en: Microorganism is recorded from 1855, with the hyphenated micro-organism appearing in the same period. The compound was formed in English rather than borrowed whole from another language.
items.cn: microorganism 记录于 1855 年，带连字符的 micro-organism 也出现在同一时期；这个复合词是在英语内部构成的，而不是从其他语言整体借入。

items.en: The word spread as improved lenses let naturalists see a world below the eye. Pasteur and Koch then linked particular microorganisms to particular diseases, giving the neutral word a medical charge.
items.cn: 随着透镜改进，博物学者看见了一个肉眼以下的世界，这个词随之传播；随后巴斯德与科赫把特定微生物与特定疾病联系起来，使这个中性词带上了医学色彩。

items.en: Viruses are smaller still and cannot reproduce without a host cell. Because they lack independent life, many authors exclude them from microorganisms, while others keep them in the loose class. The boundary is a matter of convention, not of etymology.
items.cn: 病毒更小，且离开宿主细胞无法繁殖；由于不具备独立生命，许多作者把它排除在微生物之外，也有人把它留在这个宽泛类别里。这条边界是约定问题，不是词源问题。

items.en: Recent science added microbiome and microbiota, which name whole communities rather than single cells. Microorganism now sits at the level of the individual, beside these collective terms.
items.cn: 近年的科学又加入了 microbiome 与 microbiota，它们命名的是整个群落而非单个细胞；于是 microorganism 现在处在个体的层次，与这些集体术语并列。

note.en: The first group holds spellings and derivatives built on the same compound. The second group holds everyday and technical words for small life that overlap without being equivalent.
note.cn: 第一组是同一复合词上的拼写变体与派生词；第二组是与「微小生命」相关、彼此重叠但并不等同的日常词与技术词。

entries.definition: The older British spelling with a hyphen. It means exactly the same thing and follows the nineteenth-century habit of hyphenating new compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 带连字符的英式旧拼写，意义完全相同，遵循十九世纪给新复合词加连字符的习惯。

entries.definition: The usual adjective meaning 'of microbes'. It is built on microbe rather than directly on microorganism.
entries.definitionCN: 常用形容词，意为「微生物的」；它建立在 microbe 上，而不是直接建立在 microorganism 上。

entries.definition: The study of microorganisms. The ending -logy marks a discipline, so it is not a word for a living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究微生物的学科；词尾 -logy 表示学科，因此它不是指某种生物的词。

entries.definition: A popular nineteenth-century word for a very small living thing, especially a disease-causing one. It is warmer and less formal than microorganism.
entries.definitionCN: 十九世纪的通俗词，指极小的生物、尤指致病者；比 microorganism 更口语、更不正式。

entries.definition: An everyday word for a microbe that may cause disease. It carries no scientific information about cell type or kingdom.
entries.definitionCN: 日常词，指可能致病的微生物；不包含关于细胞类型或生物界的科学信息。

entries.definition: One kind of microorganism only. Microorganism is the wider term and can cover fungi and protists that bacterium cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 只指其中一类微生物；microorganism 是更宽的词，能涵盖 bacterium 无法涵盖的真菌与原生生物。

entries.definition: Any disease-causing agent, including viruses and parasitic worms. It names a role, while microorganism names a size class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何致病因子，包括病毒与寄生蠕虫；它命名的是角色，而 microorganism 命名的是尺度类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: micro- 'small' + organism 'living body': a living body too small to see.
normal.cn: micro-「小」+ organism「生物体」：小到看不见的生物体。

normal.en: The word is a size class, not a family: bacteria, protists and fungi can all be microorganisms.
normal.cn: 这个词是尺度类别，不是科属：细菌、原生生物与真菌都可以是微生物。

normal.en: The family runs microorganism, microorganisms, micro-organism, microbial, microbiology, microbiota and microbiome.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 microorganism、microorganisms、micro-organism、microbial、microbiology、microbiota、microbiome。

normal.en: Collocations mark the habitat: soil, marine, pathogenic, beneficial and indicator microorganisms.
normal.cn: 搭配标出生境：土壤、海洋、病原、有益与指示微生物。

normal.en: A microorganism is defined by scale; a pathogen is defined by harm. The two labels can meet in one cell.
normal.cn: microorganism 按尺度定义，pathogen 按危害定义，两个标签可以落在同一个细胞上。

abstract.en: Picture a whole forest, with predators and prey, living inside one drop of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片森林连同捕食者与猎物，住在一滴水里面。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so small that a single lens must stand in for your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象一群小生命，小到必须用一枚镜片代替你的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a worker invisible to the boss who depends on it every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个老板看不见的工人，而老板每天都依赖他。

examples.en: A microorganism in the milk turned it sour before the morning.
examples.cn: 牛奶中的一种微生物在天亮前就让它变酸了。

examples.en: The team sampled the soil to count every microorganism in a gram.
examples.cn: 团队采集土壤样本，统计每克中的微生物数量。

examples.en: No microorganism was found in the sealed water sample.
examples.cn: 密封水样中没有发现任何微生物。

dict_mnemonic.text: micro-（微小）+ organism（生物体）→ 微小的生物体 → microorganism 微生物

root: 希腊 mikros「小」（阿提卡形式 smikros）→ 拉丁化前缀 micro- → 英语 micro- + organism（有机体，1825 年出现生物义）→ 1855 年合成 microorganism「微生物」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from scale to body plan, to taxonomy, to five habitats and roles: soil, sea, disease, use and indication.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从尺度走向身体构造，再走向分类，最后落到五种生境与角色：土壤、海洋、致病、利用与指示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of water under a lens, crowded with living shapes.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜片下的一滴水，挤满各种活的形状。

branches.en: SCALE AND BODY: smallness is the entry condition, and a single cell is the common body plan.
branches.cn: 尺度与身体：小是入门条件，单细胞是常见的身体构造。

branches.en: TAXONOMY: the class is defined by size, so it cuts across kingdoms and even touches the virus border.
branches.cn: 分类：这一类别按大小定义，因此横跨多个界，甚至触及病毒那条边界。

branches.en: HABITAT: the same word covers the decomposer in soil and the producer in the sea.
branches.cn: 生境：同一个词既涵盖土壤中的分解者，也涵盖海洋中的生产者。

branches.en: ROLE TOWARD HUMANS: one subset causes disease, another ferments food and makes medicine.
branches.cn: 对人的角色：一个子集致病，另一个子集发酵食物、制造药物。

branches.en: PROXY: an indicator microorganism is watched not for itself but for what its presence means.
branches.cn: 替身：监测指示微生物不是为了它本身，而是为了它的存在所意味的东西。

intro.en: Microorganism is a two-part scientific compound: a Greek prefix for smallness and a Greek-derived noun for a living body, joined in English.
intro.cn: microorganism 是两部分组成的科学复合词：表示「微小」的希腊前缀，加上希腊来源的「生物体」名词，在英语中组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Neither element is native Latin: micro- is the Latinized form of Greek mikros, and organismus is Modern/Medical Latin built on Greek organon. The compound itself was made in English, so no single Latin etymon exists.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是本族拉丁语：micro- 是希腊 mikros 的拉丁化形式，organismus 是建立在希腊 organon 上的现代或医学拉丁语。复合词本身在英语中构成，因此没有单一拉丁语词源。

items.meaning: a living thing visible only under a microscope
items.meaningCN: 只有借助显微镜才可见的生物
items.exampleCN: 一种微生物引发了这次水华。

items.example: The microbe was first seen in 1878.
items.exampleCN: 这种微生物最早于 1878 年被观察到。
微生物生命填满了这片菌席。
微生物学在 1880 年成为一门学科。
微生物学家培养了这份样本。

items.meaning: the microorganisms of a particular place
items.meaningCN: 某一特定地点的微生物群落
items.example: The gut microbiota changed with diet.
items.exampleCN: 肠道微生物群落随饮食而变。

items.meaning: the whole community and its genes
items.meaningCN: 整个微生物群落及其基因
items.example: The skin microbiome differs by site.
items.exampleCN: 皮肤微生物组因部位而异。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing small things
items.exampleCN: 显微镜使这些细胞显现出来。

latinEntries.structure: organismus, -i (m., Medical/Modern Latin, from Greek organon)

latinEntries.meaning: tool, instrument; organ of the body

definition_zh: 麦克风；传声器；话筒；窃听器
definition_en: a device that picks up sound and turns it into an electrical signal, especially the part a performer speaks into or a small hidden pickup
core_image: 一根细长的杆，把说话声收进一道看不见的电信号
scene: 演播室里，主持人把支架拉近，确认声音能送到最后一排观众的耳朵。The host leaned toward the microphone and opened the show.
sceneCN: 这里是「话筒」（第 2 个义项：供人对着说话的部件）；句意为主持人俯身靠近话筒开始节目。图中可辨识物件：话筒架、演播台、指示灯。

pos.zh: 麦克风；传声器；话筒；窃听器

derivatives.zh: 由 microphone 缩略而来，口语中读作单音节，义为「麦克风」
由 microphone 加 -ic 构成，义为「微音效应的；拾音引起的」
由 microphone 加 -y 构成，义为「微音效应」

senses.title: A device that turns sound into a signal
senses.definition: an instrument that picks up sound waves and converts them into an electrical signal
senses.definitionCN: 拾取声波并把它转换成电信号的器件
senses.example: A microphone on the table picked up every word of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的传声器把会议的每句话都收了进去。
senses.why: The Greek pieces say small sound, and early devices were built to make faint sounds audible, so the name describes catching sound rather than producing it.
senses.whyCN: 两个希腊词素说的是「微小的声音」，早期装置正是为了让微弱的声音能被听见，所以名字描述的是捕捉声音，而非发出声音。

senses.title: The part a performer speaks into
senses.definition: the part of a sound system, headset or instrument that a person speaks or sings directly into
senses.definitionCN: 音响、耳机或乐器上供人直接对着说话或演唱的部件
senses.example: She held the microphone close and lowered her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她把话筒拿近，压低声音唱。
senses.why: Once the signal device is placed in front of a performer, the word stops naming the circuit and starts naming the object aimed at the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 当这种转换器件被摆到表演者嘴前，词义就不再指电路，而开始指那个对准嘴巴的物件。

senses.title: A hidden listening device
senses.definition: a small hidden device that picks up speech so that someone can listen without being seen
senses.definitionCN: 暗藏的小型拾音装置，使人在不被看见的情况下听到谈话
senses.example: They found a microphone under the desk in the empty office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在空办公室的书桌下面发现了一个窃听器。
senses.why: A device built to catch tiny sounds is exactly what surveillance needs, so the technical name quietly took on the meaning of a bug hidden in a room.
senses.whyCN: 能捕捉细微声响的器件正是监听所需，于是这个技术名称自然而然地多了「藏在房间里的窃听器」这层意思。

intro.en: Microphone is a nineteenth-century coinage from two Greek words, small and voice, and its use moved from faint-sound devices to the electric pickup everyone knows.
intro.cn: microphone 是十九世纪用两个希腊词「小」与「声音」拼成的新词，用法从放大微弱声音的装置转到了人人熟悉的电声拾音器。

items.en: Mikros meant small or little, and it became the first element of many scientific words.
items.cn: mikros 意为小的、细微的，后来成为许多科学词汇的第一个词素。

items.en: Phone meant voice or sound, and it named both the human voice and the sound itself.
items.cn: phone 意为嗓音或声音，既指人的说话声，也指声音本身。

items.en: Writers of scientific Latin and English joined the two elements to name devices for making weak sounds easier to hear; the exact first coining is not settled.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语与英语的作者把两个词素拼起来，命名让微弱声音更容易被听见的装置；具体首见年份尚无定论。

items.en: With carbon transmitters and early telephony, the word settled on the device that converts sound into an electric current.
items.cn: 随着碳粒送话器和早期电话技术，这个词固定指把声音转换成电流的器件。

items.en: Modern English keeps the technical sense and extends it to the pickup on a headset and to a hidden listening bug.
items.cn: 现代英语保留技术义，并把它扩展到耳机上的拾音件和暗藏的窃听装置。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek voice element through short forms and compounds; the near-meaning group collects the other pieces of a sound chain.
note.cn: 形近组顺着希腊语「声音」词素，收简称与复合词；近义组收一条声音链路里的其他器件。

entries.definition: The short spoken form of microphone.
entries.definitionCN: microphone 的口语简称。

entries.definition: A device for speaking to someone at a distance; it shares the voice element.
entries.definitionCN: 远距离通话的装置，与 microphone 共用表示「声音」的词素。

entries.definition: A cone that makes a voice carry much farther.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音传得更远的锥形扩音器。

entries.definition: One of the distinct speech sounds of a language.
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言中彼此区别的语音单位。

entries.definition: A device that turns an electric signal back into sound.
entries.definitionCN: 把电信号还原成声音的装置。

entries.definition: A device that makes a signal stronger before it is sent on.
entries.definitionCN: 在信号送出前把它增强的装置。

entries.definition: A pair of earpieces with a pickup, worn on the head.
entries.definitionCN: 带拾音件的头戴式耳机。

entries.definition: The small part of a device that sits close to the ear.
entries.definitionCN: 设备上贴近耳朵的小部件。

normalIntro.en: Two Greek pieces, small and voice, were joined in the nineteenth century to name a device that catches sound.
normalIntro.cn: 两个希腊词素「小」与「声音」在十九世纪拼在一起，用来命名一种捕捉声音的器件。

normal.en: Micro- means small and -phone means voice, so the compound says small voice before it says anything technical.
normal.cn: micro- 意为「小」，-phone 意为「声音」，所以这个复合词先说的是「小声音」，然后才谈技术。

normal.en: Telephone and megaphone share the same voice element, one for distance and one for reach of volume.
normal.cn: telephone 与 megaphone 共用同一个「声音」词素，一个指距离，一个指音量传得远。

normal.en: Phoneme, phonetics and symphony all descend from the Greek word for voice.
normal.cn: phoneme、phonetics 与 symphony 都出自希腊语中表示「声音」的词。

normal.en: Audio workers write mic, not mike, for the short form, and the spelling marks the trade.
normal.cn: 音频行业把简称写作 mic 而不是 mike，这个拼写本身就是行内标记。

normal.en: A microphone converts rather than creates: the sound must exist before the device can turn it into a signal.
normal.cn: 麦克风只是转换，并不创造：声音必须先存在，器件才能把它变成信号。

abstract.en: A small voice made wide enough to fill a hall.
abstract.cn: 一个很小的声音被放大到能填满整个大厅。

abstract.en: The same pickup can serve a singer and a spy; the tool leaves the purpose to the hand that places it.
abstract.cn: 同一个拾音器可以服务歌手，也可以服务间谍；工具把用途留给摆放它的那只手。

abstract.en: Sound has no shape, yet a microphone gives it something a wire can carry.
abstract.cn: 声音本没有形状，麦克风却给了它一样能被导线带走的东西。

examples.en: She checked the microphone before the interview.
examples.cn: 采访前她检查了话筒。

examples.en: The microphone hidden in the lamp had been there for weeks.
examples.cn: 藏在台灯里的窃听器已经在那里放了好几周。

examples.en: The microphone on the stand was too far from the singer.
examples.cn: 支架上的话筒离歌手太远了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克风」——中文直接音译，麦克风就是 microphone 的常用叫法。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）与 phone（声音）拼接而成，十九世纪出现，指把声音拾取并转换为电信号的器件；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the conversion of sound into a signal; the senses divide into the pickup, the object a performer faces, and the same device used in secret.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把声音变成信号；义项分到拾音器件、表演者面对的那件物品，以及同一类器件的暗中用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin rod standing in front of a speaker, catching every word into an invisible wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细杆立在说话人面前，把每句话收进一根看不见的线。

branches.en: a faint voice made visible on a screen
branches.cn: 微弱的声音在屏幕上显成一道波形

branches.en: a singer leaning into a stand
branches.cn: 歌手俯身靠近支架

branches.en: a tiny device under a desk
branches.cn: 书桌底下的小装置

branches.en: sound caught first as a signal and then as a performance
branches.cn: 声音先被当作信号收下，再被当作表演送出

branches.en: the same pickup used openly and in secret
branches.cn: 同一个拾音器，一明一暗地用着

intro.en: A Greek prefix for small and a Greek combining form for voice sit on either side of the word, and later English shortenings and compounds extend the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「小」的希腊前缀与一个表示「声音」的希腊构词成分夹住这个词，后来的英语简称与复合词又把词族向外延伸。

latinIntro.en: The word was assembled from Greek elements in the nineteenth century, so no classical Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪用希腊词素拼出来的，古典拉丁语中没有它的同族词记录。

items.meaning: device for sound at a distance
device that makes a voice carry

definition_zh: 显微镜；高倍显微设备；严密审视
definition_en: an instrument that makes very small objects look large enough to examine; also any high-power instrument of this kind and a figurative state of close scrutiny
core_image: 一枚镜片把叶片上的小格子放大到眼前
scene: 实验台上摆着切片和光源，学生们轮流俯身看那片薄薄的叶片。Through the microscope, the leaf showed rows of tiny green cells.
sceneCN: 这里是「显微镜」（第 1 个义项：放大微小物体的仪器）；句意为透过显微镜，叶片显出成排的绿色小细胞。图中可辨识物件：显微镜、载玻片、叶片。

pos.zh: 显微镜；高倍显微设备；严密审视

collocations.zh: 在显微镜下；受到严密审视

derivatives.zh: 由 microscope 词干加 -ic 构成，义为「显微镜的；小到看不见的」
由 microscope 词干加 -y 构成，义为「显微镜术；显微检查」
由 microscope 加 -ist 构成，义为「显微镜使用者；显微镜专家」

senses.title: An instrument that magnifies small things
senses.definition: a scientific instrument with lenses that makes very small objects look large enough to examine
senses.definitionCN: 装有透镜、能把极小的物体放大到足以观察的科学仪器
senses.example: Under the microscope, the onion skin showed neat rows of cells.
senses.exampleCN: 在显微镜下，洋葱表皮显出一排排整齐的细胞。
senses.why: Greek skopein meant to look, so with mikros small the compound literally names a way of looking at what the eye cannot see, and the instrument inherited that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 skopein 意为「看」，与表示「小」的 mikros 组合，字面上就是「观看小东西的方式」，仪器便继承了这个名字。

senses.title: A high-power instrument using electrons or other radiation
senses.definition: any of the more powerful instruments that form an image with electron beams or other radiation instead of ordinary light
senses.definitionCN: 用电子束或其他辐射代替普通光成像的更高倍率的各类显微设备
senses.example: An electron microscope revealed the virus in fine detail.
senses.exampleCN: 电子显微镜把病毒的细节清晰地显现出来。
senses.why: When glass lenses reached their limit, the same word was stretched to instruments that no longer use light, because the purpose rather than the optics is what the name marks.
senses.whyCN: 当玻璃透镜放大到极限，这个词又被延伸到不再用光的仪器上，因为命名看重的是用途，而不是光学原理。

senses.title: Close, searching examination
senses.definition: a situation of being examined very closely, as in the fixed phrase under the microscope
senses.definitionCN: 处于被极为仔细检查的境地，常见于 under the microscope 这一说法
senses.example: After the leak, the whole department was under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 泄密事件之后，整个部门都处在严密审视之下。
senses.why: A microscope exposes what is invisible to the naked eye, so putting a person or an institution under one means even the smallest faults are being looked at.
senses.whyCN: 显微镜把肉眼看不见的东西摊开，因此把人或机构放在显微镜下，就等于连最细小的毛病都要被看清。

intro.en: Microscope joins two Greek words, small and to look, was given a modern Latin form, and entered English in the seventeenth century as lens-making improved.
intro.cn: microscope 把两个希腊词「小」与「看」接在一起，先有近代拉丁语形式，再在十七世纪透镜工艺进步时进入英语。

items.en: Mikros meant small, and it supplied the first element for instruments that work at a scale the eye cannot reach.
items.cn: mikros 意为小的，为那些在人眼够不着的尺度上工作的仪器提供了第一个词素。

items.en: Skopein meant to look at or examine, and its combining form -scope later named many viewing instruments.
items.cn: skopein 意为看、察看，它的构词形式 -scope 后来命名了许多观察仪器。

items.en: Early scientists gave the new instrument a Latin name from the two Greek elements before any English word existed for it.
items.cn: 早期的科学家用这两个希腊词素给新仪器起了拉丁名，当时英语里还没有对应的词。

items.en: English adopted the word in the seventeenth century as lens grinding made single-lens instruments practical for naturalists.
items.cn: 十七世纪，随着透镜研磨技术让单透镜仪器对博物学者变得实用，英语采纳了这个词。

items.en: The compound now covers electron and other advanced instruments, and its prepositional phrase has become a metaphor for close scrutiny.
items.cn: 这个复合词现在涵盖了电子显微镜等进阶设备，它的介词短语也成了「严密审视」的比喻说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the small plus look pattern and its derived family; the near-meaning group collects the glass and the specimens that go with the instrument.
note.cn: 形近组顺着「小」加「看」的构词模式与派生词族；近义组收与这种仪器配套的镜片和标本。

entries.definition: Too small to be seen without an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 小到不用仪器就看不见的。

entries.definition: The technique of examining things with a microscope.
entries.definitionCN: 用显微镜检查事物的技术。

entries.definition: An instrument for viewing distant objects.
entries.definitionCN: 观察远处物体的仪器。

entries.definition: An instrument for looking over or around an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 越过或绕过障碍观察的仪器。

entries.definition: A curved piece of glass that bends light to form an image.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲的玻璃片，使光折射成像。

entries.definition: A hand-held lens used to make small things look larger.
entries.definitionCN: 手持透镜，把小的东西放大来看。

entries.definition: A thin glass plate on which a specimen is placed for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 放置标本供观察的薄玻璃片。

entries.definition: A small sample of something kept for study.
entries.definitionCN: 留作研究用的少量样品。

normalIntro.en: Small plus looking: the compound names an instrument that does not enlarge the object but brings it close enough for the eye.
normalIntro.cn: 「小」加「看」：这个复合词命名的仪器并不把物体变大，而是把它拉到眼睛够得近的地方。

normal.en: Micro- means small and -scope comes from the Greek verb for looking, so the word spells out looking at small things.
normal.cn: micro- 意为「小」，-scope 出自希腊语中表示「看」的动词，这个词把「看小东西」直接拼了出来。

normal.en: Telescope uses the same -scope element for far objects, and periscope uses it for looking around.
normal.cn: telescope 用同一个 -scope 词素看远处，periscope 用它绕过障碍看。

normal.en: Microscopic adds -ic and describes what is too small for the unaided eye.
normal.cn: microscopic 加了 -ic，形容小到肉眼无法看清的东西。

normal.en: Microscopy names the technique, and a microscopist is the person who performs it.
normal.cn: microscopy 指这门技术，microscopist 指操作它的人。

normal.en: Under the microscope is a fixed phrase that moved from the lab bench into everyday talk about scrutiny.
normal.cn: under the microscope 是固定说法，已经从实验台走进日常语言，指严密审查。

abstract.en: The glass does not enlarge the cell; it only shortens the distance between the cell and your attention.
abstract.cn: 镜片并不把细胞变大，只是缩短了细胞与你注意力之间的距离。

abstract.en: Looking closely rewrites what you see: a plain leaf becomes rows of green rooms.
abstract.cn: 凑近看会改写你所见的：一片普通的叶子变成一排排绿色的小房间。

abstract.en: A lens became a word for scrutiny, because attention magnifies faults just as glass magnifies cells.
abstract.cn: 一片镜片变成了「审视」的代名词，因为注意力放大过失，就像镜片放大细胞一样。

examples.en: The students took turns looking through the microscope.
examples.cn: 学生们轮流透过显微镜观察。

examples.en: An electron microscope can show the shape of a virus.
examples.cn: 电子显微镜能显示病毒的形状。

examples.en: After the audit, the whole office was under the microscope.
examples.cn: 审计之后，整个办公室都处在严密审视之下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克看」——麦克凑近镜片看小虫，看小东西的镜子就是显微镜。

root: 希腊语 mikros（小）与 skopein（看）拼接，经近代科学拉丁语 microscopium 进入英语，指观察微小物体的仪器；没有可靠的古典拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is looking at what is too small; the senses divide into the lens instrument, the powered instruments that replaced light, and the scrutiny those instruments symbolize.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「观看过小的东西」；义项分到透镜仪器、取代光的强力设备，以及这类仪器所象征的严密审视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single lens bringing the cells of a leaf close enough for the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚镜片把叶片上的细胞拉到眼前。

branches.en: onion cells lined up under a lens
branches.cn: 透镜下排成行的洋葱细胞

branches.en: an electron beam tracing a virus
branches.cn: 电子束扫出病毒的轮廓

branches.en: a department watched after a leak
branches.cn: 泄密之后被盯住的部门

branches.en: detail revealed first by light and then by electrons
branches.cn: 细节先由光显现，再由电子显现

branches.en: the same act of looking closely, at cells and at people
branches.cn: 同一个凑近细看的动作，一次对细胞，一次对人

intro.en: A Greek prefix for small and a Greek look-element form the word, and English suffixes later build the technique and the person around it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「小」的希腊前缀与一个表示「看」的希腊词素构成这个词，英语后缀后来又在它周围造出技术与人的名称。

latinIntro.en: The word was formed from Greek elements and given a modern Latin shape by early scientists, so no classical Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词由希腊词素构成，早期科学家只给了它一个近代拉丁语外形，古典拉丁语中没有同族词记录。

definition_zh: 偏头痛；偏头痛发作
definition_en: a severe headache that often throbs on one side of the head and comes with nausea and a dislike of light
core_image: 一侧太阳穴里藏着一把小锤，光一亮就敲一下
scene: 下午的光线突然变强，她拉上窗帘，抱着头缩进沙发角落。A single bright shaft of light made her migraine worse within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 migraine 是「一次偏头痛发作」（第 2 个义项：正在发生的那一阵头痛）；句意为一道强光在几分钟内就让她的偏头痛加重了。

pos.zh: 偏头痛；偏头痛发作

collocations.zh: 静默型偏头痛（只有先兆、不头痛）

derivatives.zh: 偏头痛的；患偏头痛的；由 migraine 加 -ous 构成
偏头痛患者；借法语 -eur（指人）加在 migraine 之后
抗偏头痛的；anti-（抗）加 migraine，多用于描述药物

senses.title: The recurring headache disorder
senses.titleCN: 偏头痛（反复发作的头痛疾病）
senses.definition: a neurological condition that causes repeated severe headaches, often on one side of the head and often with nausea
senses.definitionCN: 引起反复剧烈头痛的神经系统疾病，痛常在单侧，并常伴恶心
senses.example: Migraine runs in her family, and two of her sisters have it too.
senses.exampleCN: 偏头痛在她家有遗传，她的两个姐妹也有。
senses.why: The Greek name meant half the skull, so the disorder was named for where it hurts rather than for what causes it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原名意为「半边颅骨」，所以这个病是按「痛在哪里」命名的，而不是按病因命名。

senses.title: A single attack
senses.definition: one episode of throbbing pain, usually lasting hours, sometimes with vomiting
senses.definitionCN: 一次搏动性的疼痛发作，通常持续数小时，有时伴呕吐
senses.example: A migraine kept her in a dark room all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 一次偏头痛让她整个下午都待在暗房里。
senses.why: Patients feel the disorder only during an attack, so the same noun names both the illness and the episode.
senses.whyCN: 患者只在发作时才感到这个病，所以同一个词既指疾病，也指那一次发作。

senses.title: Migraine with aura
senses.definition: a migraine preceded by flashing lights, a blind spot or tingling that warns of the coming pain
senses.definitionCN: 在疼痛到来之前出现闪光、视野缺口或刺麻感的偏头痛
senses.example: Her migraine with aura always begins with a zigzag of light.
senses.exampleCN: 她的有先兆偏头痛总是以一道锯齿状的光开始。
senses.why: The warning signals come from the brain itself, so doctors gave the word a subtype that names the visible omen.
senses.whyCN: 这些警告信号来自大脑本身，于是医生给这个词添了一个亚型，专门命名看得见的「前兆」。

senses.title: Silent migraine
senses.definition: an attack with the aura and the nausea but without the headache itself
senses.definitionCN: 有先兆与恶心、却没有头痛本身的一次发作
senses.example: A silent migraine can be mistaken for a stomach upset.
senses.exampleCN: 静默型偏头痛可能被误当成肠胃不适。
senses.why: Because the headache can be absent, the word had to carry a form that describes the attack by its other symptoms.
senses.whyCN: 因为头痛可以缺席，这个词只好多出一个用法，靠其他症状来描述这次发作。

senses.title: The old name for half the head
senses.definition: the older medical name hemicrania, which simply described pain in one half of the head
senses.definitionCN: 较早的医学名称 hemicrania，字面只说「半边头在痛」
senses.example: Old texts called it hemicrania before the French form became migraine.
senses.exampleCN: 在法语形式变成 migraine 之前，旧文献称它为 hemicrania。
senses.why: The modern word is a worn-down French version of the Greek half-head name, so the oldest layer still shows through.
senses.whyCN: 现代这个词是希腊语「半头」之名经法语磨损后的样子，最古老的那一层至今仍透出来。

intro.en: Migraine is the worn-down descendant of Greek hemikrania, a compound of hemi-, half, and kranion, skull.
intro.cn: migraine 是希腊语 hemikrania 磨损后的后代，那个词由 hemi-（一半）与 kranion（颅骨）复合而成。

items.en: Hemi- meant half, and it still halves words such as hemisphere.
items.cn: hemi- 意为「一半」，至今仍把 hemisphere 之类的词一分为二。

items.en: Kranion meant the skull or the head, and it survives in cranium.
items.cn: kranion 指颅骨或头部，至今留在 cranium 一词里。

items.en: Hemikrania named a pain that occupied one half of the head, a term used in Greek medical writing.
items.cn: hemikrania 指占据半边头颅的疼痛，是希腊医学文献里的用语。

items.en: Medical Latin took the Greek term over almost unchanged.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语几乎原样接收了这个希腊词。

items.en: French wore the long word down to migraigne, losing the hemi- that speakers no longer recognised.
items.cn: 法语把这个长词磨成 migraigne，丢掉了听者已不再辨认的 hemi-。

items.en: English borrowed the French form as migrayne, and the modern spelling migraine settled later.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 migrayne，现代拼写 migraine 则是后来才固定的。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the half-head root and its modern family, while the near-meaning group places migraine among other headaches.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「半头」这个词根及其现代词族；近义组把偏头痛放进其他头痛之中。

entries.definition: relating to or affected by migraine
entries.definitionCN: 偏头痛的；患偏头痛的；由 migraine 加 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: pain in one half of the head, the old name for migraine
entries.definitionCN: 半边头的疼痛，是偏头痛的旧名；与 migraine 同源。

entries.definition: a person who suffers from migraine
entries.definitionCN: 偏头痛患者；借法语后缀 -eur 指人。

entries.definition: pain in the head from any cause
entries.definitionCN: 任何原因引起的头痛，范围比偏头痛宽得多。

entries.definition: a headache that strikes in short, extremely painful bursts around one eye
entries.definitionCN: 围绕一只眼睛短促爆发的剧痛，属于另一种原发性头痛。

entries.definition: a medical word for headache of any kind
entries.definitionCN: 医学上对任何头痛的称呼，并不专指偏头痛。

normalIntro.en: Migraine is a worn-down Greek phrase for half the skull, so the word itself explains why the pain favours one side.
normalIntro.cn: migraine 是希腊语「半边颅骨」磨损后的样子，词本身就解释了疼痛为何偏爱一侧。

normal.en: Hemi- means half and kranion means skull, so hemicrania is literally half-head pain.
normal.cn: hemi- 是一半，kranion 是颅骨，hemicrania 字面就是「半边头在痛」。

normal.en: French shortened hemicrania to migraigne, and English took that shorter form.
normal.cn: 法语把 hemicrania 缩短成 migraigne，英语取的是这个较短的形式。

normal.en: Migrainous is the adjective, and a migraineur is the person who has the attacks.
normal.cn: migrainous 是形容词，migraineur 指经常发作的那个人。

normal.en: An attack is one episode, while chronic migraine is the pattern of frequent attacks.
normal.cn: an attack 是一次发作，而 chronic migraine 指频繁发作的模式。

normal.en: A silent migraine has the aura without the headache, so the name covers a whole family of attacks.
normal.cn: 静默型偏头痛有先兆而无头痛，可见这个名字覆盖的是一整个发作类型。

abstract.en: Picture a vice closing on one temple while the other side stays free.
abstract.cn: 想象一把虎钳夹住一侧太阳穴，另一侧却毫无感觉。

abstract.en: Imagine a dark room, a cold cloth over the eyes, and a wave of nausea.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗房、一块敷在眼睛上的冷布，还有一阵恶心。

abstract.en: Think of a zigzag of light crawling across the view before the pain arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一道锯齿状的光在疼痛到来之前爬过视野。

examples.en: She has had migraines since her teens, usually on the right side.
examples.cn: 她从十几岁起就常犯偏头痛，多发生在右侧。

examples.en: Bright light and skipped meals can trigger a migraine.
examples.cn: 强光和错过吃饭都可能诱发偏头痛。

examples.en: Migraine with aura is often preceded by flashing lights.
examples.cn: 有先兆偏头痛常以闪光作为前奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「my grain」——像脑袋里有一粒麦子被磨盘来回碾过，碾得半边发痛；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hēmi-（一半）+ kranion（颅骨）→ hēmikrania（半边头之痛）→ 拉丁语 hemicrania → 古法语 migraigne → 英语 migraine，核心义「只痛半边头」。

sensesIntro.en: Migraine names a disorder, then a single attack, then the aura and the headache-free form, and it still carries the Greek half-head description.
sensesIntro.cn: migraine 先指一种疾病，再指一次发作，又指有先兆与无头痛的类型，而它始终带着希腊语「半头」的描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small hammer behind one temple that strikes whenever light flashes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一侧太阳穴后面藏着一把小锤，光一闪就敲一下。

branches.en: The disorder is the long condition behind every attack.
branches.cn: 疾病是每一次发作背后那个长期存在的状况。

branches.en: One attack is the disorder felt at a single moment.
branches.cn: 一次发作是这种病在某一刻被感受到的样子。

branches.en: The aura is the warning the brain gives before the pain.
branches.cn: 先兆是大脑在疼痛之前给出的警告。

branches.en: Without the headache, the attack shows only its other symptoms.
branches.cn: 头痛缺席时，这次发作只剩下别的症状。

branches.en: The Greek half-head name and the modern disorder describe the same place of pain.
branches.cn: 希腊语的「半头」之名与今天的疾病，说的是同一个疼痛位置。

intro.en: Migraine is the worn-down French descendant of Greek hemikrania, and hemi- still halves many English words.
intro.cn: migraine 是希腊语 hemikrania 经法语磨损后的后代，而 hemi- 至今仍把许多英语词分成两半。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept hemicrania and cranium, and the Latin cranium is the same skull that Greek kranion named.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语保留了 hemicrania 与 cranium，而拉丁语的 cranium 就是希腊语 kranion 所指的那块颅骨。

items.meaningCN: 发作于一侧的反复头痛

items.exampleCN: 偏头痛患者；业余爱好者

latinEntries.example: Hemicrania is the Latin form of the Greek name.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hemicrania 是那个希腊名称的拉丁形式。
cranium 生出 cranial 与 craniology。

definition_zh: 迁移；迁徙；移居；（数据、系统）迁移；（细胞）移动
definition_en: to move from one place, habitat or system to another, especially over a distance and often for a season or a new life
core_image: 一群身影越过旧地平线，走向另一条尚未抵达的地平线
scene: 这里指「迁移」。 Every October the birds migrate south along the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 migrate 是「迁徙」（第 1 个义项：动物随季节从一处栖息地移到另一处）；句意：每年十月，鸟群沿着海岸向南迁徙。场景要点：一条海岸线、排成人字的鸟群、地平线上尚未到达的南方。

pos.zh: 迁移；迁徙；移居（常与 from、to 连用）
（信息技术）迁移（数据、系统、账户）

collocations.zh: 在两个地方之间来回迁移

derivatives.zh: 迁移；迁徙；移居
移民；候鸟；迁徙的
迁徙的；有迁徙习性的
移出；迁离本国
移入；迁入某国定居
转世；跨地域迁移

senses.title: Animals on the move
senses.titleCN: 动物迁徙：随季节换一片栖息地
senses.definition: of animals, to move from one habitat or region to another at a distance, usually with the seasons
senses.definitionCN: 指动物远距离地从一处栖息地或地区移到另一处，通常随季节而行
senses.example: Every October the birds migrate south along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 每年十月，鸟群沿着海岸向南迁徙。
senses.why: The animal sense is recorded from 1753. Latin migrare already meant 'to move from one place to another', and birds made the word's clearest picture.
senses.whyCN: 动物义项自 1753 年有记录。拉丁语 migrare 本就意为“从一处移到另一处”，而鸟群给这个词提供了最清晰的画面。

senses.title: People settle elsewhere
senses.definition: of people, to move from one place of residence to another at a distance, especially to another country
senses.definitionCN: 指人远距离地从一处居住地迁到另一处，尤指迁往另一个国家
senses.example: Her grandparents migrated to the coast in the 1950s.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母在 20 世纪 50 年代移居到了海边。
senses.why: The sense for persons is recorded by 1770. The same movement now carries a household, a language and a future, not only a body.
senses.whyCN: 指人的义项在 1770 年已有记录。同一种移动现在承载的是一个家庭、一门语言和一种未来，而不只是一具身体。

senses.title: Move from place to place
senses.titleCN: 一般移动：只说到从一处到另一处
senses.definition: to pass from one place or position to another, without stressing either departure or arrival
senses.definitionCN: 从一处或一个位置移到另一处，既不强调离开，也不强调抵达
senses.example: The infection migrated from the skin to the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 感染从皮肤转移到了关节。
senses.why: This is the word's first English sense, recorded in the 1690s: 'to pass from one place to another'. It is the plain trunk from which the other senses branch.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词在英语里的第一个义项，1690 年代有记录：“从一处移到另一处”。它是其他义项分叉出来的那根主干。

senses.title: Data and systems
senses.titleCN: 数据与系统迁移：换一个平台继续运行
senses.definition: in computing, to move data, programs or services from one system or platform to another
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，把数据、程序或服务从一个系统或平台移到另一个
senses.example: The company will migrate its accounts to the new platform in June.
senses.exampleCN: 公司将在六月把账户迁移到新平台。
senses.why: The old picture fits exactly: something alive in one place is picked up and set down in another, and must keep working after the move.
senses.whyCN: 旧画面严丝合缝：在一个地方运行着的东西被拿起、放到另一个地方，而且搬完之后还得继续运行。

senses.title: Cells and substances
senses.definition: in biology and medicine, of cells or substances, to move within the body or from one tissue to another
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学与医学中，指细胞或物质在体内移动，或从一种组织移到另一种
senses.example: These cells migrate to the wound and begin repairing it.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞迁移到伤口处并开始修复。
senses.why: The distance shrinks to millimetres, but the verb keeps its shape: a body leaves one site and arrives at another.
senses.whyCN: 距离缩短到毫米级，但动词的形状没变：一个个体离开一处，抵达另一处。

senses.title: Labour on the move
senses.titleCN: 劳动力流动：为生计迁往别处
senses.definition: of workers or populations, to move from one region to another in search of work or better conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指工人或人群为寻找工作或更好的条件而从一地区迁往另一地区
senses.example: Whole villages migrated to the cities when the factories opened.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂开工后，整村整村的人迁往城市。
senses.why: When migration is driven by wages, the word stops describing nature and starts describing economics.
senses.whyCN: 当迁徙由工资驱动时，这个词就不再描述自然，而开始描述经济。

senses.title: Switch to a new way
senses.titleCN: 比喻：转向新的做法或平台
senses.definition: figuratively, to change from one practice, model or system to another
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：从一种做法、模式或制度转到另一种
senses.example: Many readers have migrated from print to podcasts.
senses.exampleCN: 许多读者已经从纸媒转向播客。
senses.why: The journey no longer has geography, only a before and an after. The verb survives because the feeling of relocation survives.
senses.whyCN: 这趟旅程不再有地理，只剩下“之前”与“之后”。动词之所以还活着，是因为那种搬迁的感觉还活着。

senses.title: Round trip
senses.titleCN: 循环迁徙：去了还会回来
senses.definition: to move regularly between two places, as migratory birds or pastoral families do
senses.definitionCN: 像候鸟或游牧家庭那样，在两处之间规律地往返
senses.example: The herders migrate between the lowlands in winter and the high pastures in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 牧民冬天迁到低地，夏天迁往高山牧场。
senses.why: Not every migration is one-way. The word covers the round trip as easily as the exodus, because it names the moving, not the staying.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有迁徙都是单向的。这个词既能指一去不返的大迁徙，也能指往返循环，因为它命名的是“移动”，而不是“留下”。

senses.title: Direction left open
senses.titleCN: 用法分界：不指明移出还是移入
senses.definition: used without specifying whether one is leaving a place or arriving at one, unlike emigrate and immigrate
senses.definitionCN: 使用时不明说自己是离开某地还是抵达某地，这与 emigrate 和 immigrate 不同
senses.example: The report says people migrate for work, without asking which border they cross.
senses.exampleCN: 报告说人们为工作而迁移，并不追问他们越过的是哪一道边界。
senses.why: The Century Dictionary put it plainly in 1897: migrate stresses the change itself, not the place of departure or of stopping. Emigrate looks back, immigrate looks forward.
senses.whyCN: 《世纪词典》1897 年说得很清楚：migrate 强调变化本身，而不强调出发地或落脚地。emigrate 回头看，immigrate 向前看。

intro.en: Migrate comes from Latin migrare 'to move from one place to another', probably from PIE *(e)meigw- 'to change'. Its English life began with the plain sense 'pass from one place to another' and later specialised into animals, people and machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migrate 来自拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”，可能源自原始印欧语 *(e)meigw-“改变”。它在英语里先有“从一处到另一处”的平实义，后来才分化出动物、人与机器诸义。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to pass from one place to another', from Latin migratus, past participle of migrare 'to move from one place to another'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 90 年代，意为“从一处移到另一处”，来自拉丁语 migratus，即 migrare“从一处移到另一处”的过去分词。

items.en: Latin migrare is probably originally *migwros, from PIE *(e)meigw- 'to change', an extended form of the root *mei- (1) 'to change, go, move'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 migrare 最初大概是 *migwros，来自原始印欧语 *(e)meigw-“改变”，而这是词根 *mei-（第一支）“改变、走、移动”的扩展形式。

items.en: Of animals, 'to remove from one habitat to another at a distance' is recorded. The word's most familiar picture, a flock crossing a season, is fixed here.
items.cn: 记录到指动物的“远距离地从一处栖息地移到另一处”。这个词最熟悉的画面——一群鸟越过一个季节——在这里固定下来。

items.en: Of persons, 'to pass or remove from one place of residence to another at a distance' is recorded, especially from one country to another.
items.cn: 记录到指人的“远距离地从一处居住地迁到另一处”，尤指从一个国家到另一个国家。

items.en: The Century Dictionary draws the line still taught today: migrate stresses the change, not the departure or the stopping place; emigrate views the person leaving, immigrate views the person arriving.
items.cn: 《世纪词典》划出了今天仍在教的界线：migrate 强调变化，而不强调出发地或落脚地；emigrate 着眼于离开的人，immigrate 着眼于抵达的人。

items.en: The computing sense, to move data or services to another system, extends the old picture into machines. The family keeps its bearings: migration (1610s), migrant (1760), emigrate (1778), immigrate (1620s).
items.cn: 计算机义“把数据或服务迁到另一系统”把旧画面延伸到机器上。这个词族的方向感仍在：migration（17 世纪 10 年代）、migrant（1760）、emigrate（1778）、immigrate（17 世纪 20 年代）。

note.en: The first group is the family built on migrate: the process, the person or animal, and the adjective. The second group separates the words that name a move with a direction, which migrate deliberately leaves out.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 migrate 上的词族：过程、人（或动物）、形容词。第二组区分那些带方向的“迁移”词，而 migrate 恰恰有意不指明方向。

entries.definition: the act or process of migrating, or a group of people or animals doing it. It is the noun of the event, not a synonym of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 迁移的行为或过程，或正在迁移的一群人或动物。它是这一事件的名词，不是动词的同义词。

entries.definition: a person or animal that migrates, or an adjective meaning 'migratory'. It names the mover, while migrate names the moving.
entries.definitionCN: 迁移的人或动物，也可作形容词表示“迁徙的”。它命名的是移动者，而 migrate 命名的是移动本身。

entries.definition: having the habit of migrating, as a species or a way of life. It describes the pattern, not a single journey.
entries.definitionCN: 有迁徙习性的，如某个物种或某种生活方式。它描述的是模式，而不是某一趟旅程。

entries.definition: relating to migration. It is rare and mostly replaced by migratory, but it keeps the noun's abstract frame.
entries.definitionCN: 与迁移有关的。它很少用，多半被 migratory 取代，但仍保留名词的抽象框架。

entries.definition: to leave one's own country and settle elsewhere. The prefix e- is Latin ex- 'out': it views the person from the place left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国到别处定居。前缀 e- 即拉丁语 ex-“向外”：它从被留下的那个地方看这个人。

entries.definition: to come into a country to settle there. The prefix im- is Latin in- 'into': it views the person from the place of arrival.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某国并在此定居。前缀 im- 即拉丁语 in-“进入”：它从抵达地看这个人。

entries.definition: to move to a new location, often with an employer or a company. It is more administrative than migrate and usually one-way and planned.
entries.definitionCN: 搬到新地点，常指随雇主或公司搬迁。它比 migrate 更带行政色彩，通常是单向且有计划的。

entries.definition: to migrate across or through something, and in religion to pass into another body after death. The prefix trans- 'across' adds a crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 跨越某地迁移；在宗教中也指死后灵魂转入另一具身体。前缀 trans-“横越”加了一层“穿过”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin migrare 'to move from one place to another', the PIE root *mei- 'to go, change', and the direction-marked family emigrate, immigrate, transmigrate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”、原始印欧语词根 *mei-“走、改变”，以及带方向标记的 emigrate、immigrate、transmigrate。

normal.en: migr- means 'move from one place to another'. Migrate is the bare movement, with no prefix telling you which way.
normal.cn: migr- 表示“从一处移到另一处”。migrate 是光秃秃的移动，没有前缀告诉你方向。

normal.en: emigrate has e- (ex-, 'out'): you leave. immigrate has im- (in-, 'into'): you arrive. The same journey looks different from each end.
normal.cn: emigrate 带 e-（ex-，“向外”）：你离开。immigrate 带 im-（in-，“进入”）：你抵达。同一趟旅程，从两端看不一样。

normal.en: migration is the event, migrant is the mover, migratory is the habit. Three forms, three jobs.
normal.cn: migration 是事件，migrant 是移动者，migratory 是习性。三个形式，三份工作。

normal.en: The root may be PIE *(e)meigw- 'to change', linked to *mei- 'to go, move'. Latin migrare is the branch that reached English.
normal.cn: 词根可能是原始印欧语 *(e)meigw-“改变”，与 *mei-“走、移动”相关。拉丁语 migrare 是抵达英语的那一支。

normal.en: Computing borrowed the bird: data migrate to a new platform the way flocks move to a new coast.
normal.cn: 计算机借用了鸟：数据迁到新平台，就像鸟群迁到一片新的海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a coastline at dusk and a line of wings crossing the last of the light. Nothing in the picture says whether they will come back.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏的海岸线，以及一排翅膀划过最后一点光。这幅画里没有任何东西说明它们会不会回来。

abstract.en: Migration is measured from the mover, not from the border. That is why the same person is an emigrant to one country and an immigrant to another.
abstract.cn: 迁徙是从移动者身上度量的，不是从边界度量的。所以同一个人对一国是移出者，对另一国是移入者。

abstract.en: The word travels as far as its picture: birds, workers, cells, files. Wherever something leaves one place and keeps living in another, migrate still fits.
abstract.cn: 这个词跟着它的画面走得一样远：鸟、工人、细胞、文件。只要某物离开一处并在另一处继续存活，migrate 就仍然适用。

examples.en: The whales migrate thousands of kilometres to breed in warmer water.
examples.cn: 鲸鱼迁徙数千公里，到更温暖的水域繁殖。

examples.en: Her family migrated from the north to the coast three generations ago.
examples.cn: 她家三代以前从北方迁到了海边。

examples.en: The archive will migrate to a new server over the weekend.
examples.cn: 档案库将在周末迁移到新的服务器上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “买格瑞特”——买张票，格瑞特就跨过边界去了另一片土地 → migrate 迁移、迁徙（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”，核心是“离开一块地面，落到另一块地面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of migrate, all from one motion: a body leaves one place and arrives at another. The word never says which end matters, which is why birds, workers, cells and files can all use it.
sensesIntro.cn: migrate 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：一个个体离开一处，抵达另一处。这个词从不说哪一端更重要，所以鸟、工人、细胞与文件都能用它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group crossing from one horizon to another, with the departure and the arrival equally unnamed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群身影从一条地平线越向另一条，出发地与抵达地同样不被点名。

chain: THE MOVE ITSELF IS THE WORD

branches.en: SEASONS: animals and herders move on a rhythm, and the journey may be a round trip rather than an exit.
branches.cn: 季节：动物与牧民按节奏移动，这趟旅程可能是往返，而不是出走。

branches.en: HOUSEHOLDS: people move to settle or to work, and the move carries a family or a labour force.
branches.cn: 家庭：人为定居或为工作而移动，这一移动承载的是一个家庭或一支劳动力。

branches.en: PLAIN MOTION: the oldest sense describes movement without direction, which is exactly what separates it from emigrate and immigrate.
branches.cn: 平实移动：最老的义项描述无方向的移动，这正是它与 emigrate、immigrate 的分界。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: data and habits change platforms, and the old geography becomes a before and an after.
branches.cn: 系统：数据与习惯更换平台，旧的地理变成“之前”与“之后”。

branches.en: THE BODY: cells make the same journey at millimetre scale, from one tissue to another.
branches.cn: 身体：细胞以毫米尺度完成同一趟旅程，从一种组织到另一种。

intro.en: Migrate is Latin migr- 'move, shift' plus the verb ending -ate. Direction is added by prefixes: e- 'out', im- 'in', trans- 'across'. English also builds -ion, -ant and -ory nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: migrate 是拉丁语 migr-“移动、迁徙”加动词词尾 -ate。方向由前缀补充：e-“向外”、im-“向内”、trans-“横越”。英语还用 -ion、-ant、-ory 构成名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin migrare 'to move from one place to another' gives the stem; migratio gives migration and migrans gives migrant. The family is Latin throughout, with no Greek element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”提供词干；migratio 给出 migration，migrans 给出 migrant。这个词族从头到尾都是拉丁语，没有希腊语成分。

items.meaning: to move from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 从一处移到另一处（migr- 移动 + -ate 动词词尾）
items.example: Some species migrate only once in a lifetime.
items.exampleCN: 有些物种一生只迁徙一次。

items.meaning: the act or process of moving to another place
items.meaningCN: 迁移；迁徙（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The migration takes three generations to complete.
items.exampleCN: 这场迁徙要三代人才能完成。

items.meaningCN: 迁徙者；移民（-ant 表示施动者）
items.example: The camp houses migrant workers from four provinces.
items.exampleCN: 营地里住着来自四个省份的务工移民。

items.meaningCN: 有迁徙习性的；迁徙的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The wetland is a stopover for migratory birds.
items.exampleCN: 这片湿地是候鸟的中转站。

items.meaning: to leave one's country and settle elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 移出；迁离本国（e- 向外 + migrate）
items.exampleCN: 他的父母在 1979 年移居国外。

items.meaning: to come into a country and settle
items.meaningCN: 移入；迁入定居（im- 向内 + migrate）
items.example: They immigrated with two suitcases and no English.
items.exampleCN: 他们带着两只箱子、一句英语也不会就迁了进来。

items.meaning: to pass across or into another body or place
items.meaningCN: 跨越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 横越 + migrate）
items.example: The doctrine says the soul transmigrates after death.
items.exampleCN: 该教义说灵魂在死后转世。

items.meaning: a person who leaves a country
items.example: The ship carried emigrants to the south.
items.exampleCN: 这艘船把移出者载往南方。

items.meaning: a person who comes to settle in a country
items.example: The city grew fast on immigrant labour.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市靠移民劳动力迅速扩张。

items.meaning: the act of leaving one's country
items.meaningCN: 移出；迁离（e- 向外 + migration）
items.exampleCN: 人口迁出使高地村庄空了下来。

items.meaning: the act of entering and settling in a country
items.meaningCN: 移入；迁入定居（im- 向内 + migration）
items.example: Immigration rules changed again last spring.
items.exampleCN: 移民入境规定去年春天又变了。

items.meaning: a passing across, or the passing of a soul into another body
items.meaningCN: 跨越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 横越 + migration）
items.example: Transmigration is central to the doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 转世之说在该教义中处于核心位置。

latinEntries.meaning: to move from one place to another

definition_zh: 迁移；移居；迁徙；移民潮；数据迁移；细胞迁移；污染物迁移；劳动力流动；系统间转移
definition_en: the movement of people, animals or other things from one place, region or system to another, especially over a long distance or in large numbers
core_image: 暮色中一群鸟排成人字，从一片湿地飞向另一片湿地
scene: 这里指「迁移」。 At dusk the birds form a wedge and leave one marsh for another: their movement is migration.
sceneCN: 这里 migration 是「迁徙」（第 2 个义项：动物迁徙）；句意：暮色中鸟群排成人字，离开一片湿地飞向另一片湿地，它们的移动就是迁徙。图中可辨识物件：人字形鸟群、起飞的湿地、远处的湿地、暮色天空、芦苇。

pos.zh: 迁移；移居；迁徙；移民潮；数据迁移

forms.label: 单数（一次迁移或迁移这件事）
复数（多批迁移或多条迁徙路线）

derivatives.zh: 迁移；迁徙；移居
迁移者；移民；候鸟
迁徙的；流动的
移入；移民入境
移出；移民出境

senses.title: People moving to a new place to live
senses.titleCN: 人的迁移：搬到另一处生活
senses.definition: the movement of people from one place or country to another in order to settle there
senses.definitionCN: 人们从一个地方或国家移到另一个地方或国家定居
senses.example: Migration from the countryside to the cities changed the labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 从乡村向城市的迁移改变了劳动力市场。
senses.why: Latin migrare means to move from one place to another, and migratio names that moving. Applied to people, the change of place becomes a change of home.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 migrare 意为从一处移到另一处，migratio 指这一移动。用在人身上，换地方就变成了换家。

senses.title: Animal migration: seasonal movement between regions
senses.titleCN: 动物迁徙：随季节在区域间移动
senses.definition: the seasonal movement of animals, birds or fish from one region to another and often back again
senses.definitionCN: 动物、鸟类或鱼类随季节从一个地区移到另一地区，且常常再返回
senses.example: The migration of the geese follows the river valley every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天雁群的迁徙都沿着河谷走。
senses.why: The same verb fits animals because they also leave one place for another. The word adds nothing about distance; the round trip and the season are supplied by context.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也适用于动物，因为它们同样离开一处去另一处。词本身不涉及距离；往返与季节是由语境提供的。

senses.title: A wave of movement: numbers on the move
senses.definition: a large-scale movement of people or animals considered as a quantity or a trend
senses.definitionCN: 被当作数量或趋势来看待的大规模人潮或兽群移动
senses.example: The century saw a migration of millions across the border.
senses.exampleCN: 那个世纪有数百万人越过边境迁移。
senses.why: Once many journeys are counted together, migration stops being one person's move and becomes a demographic event, measured and graphed by agencies.
senses.whyCN: 当许多趟行程被一起计数，migration 就不再是一个人的搬家，而成为一个人口事件，被机构测量并绘成图表。

senses.title: Data migration: moving information between systems
senses.titleCN: 数据迁移：把信息搬到另一套系统
senses.definition: the transfer of data from one storage system, format or platform to another
senses.definitionCN: 把数据从一种存储系统、格式或平台转移到另一种
senses.example: The data migration took three nights and two rollbacks.
senses.exampleCN: 这次数据迁移用了三个夜晚和两次回滚。
senses.why: Computing keeps the literal image: records that lived in one place are moved to another. The risk is the same as in any move, that something is lost on the way.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域保留了字面意象：原本住在一处的记录被搬到另一处。风险也跟任何搬家一样：路上可能丢东西。

senses.title: Cell migration: cells moving through tissue
senses.titleCN: 细胞迁移：细胞在组织中移动
senses.definition: in biology, the directed movement of cells through tissue, as in wound healing or development
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指细胞在组织中定向移动，如伤口愈合或发育过程中的移动
senses.example: Cell migration is central to how wounds close.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞迁移是伤口如何闭合的核心环节。
senses.why: Biology applies the word at a scale invisible to the eye. A cell leaves one position for another, so the same migrare serves, with the 'journey' compressed to micrometres.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个词用在肉眼不可见的尺度。细胞离开一个位置去另一个位置，所以同一个 migrare 仍然适用，只是「行程」被压缩到微米级。

senses.title: Pollutant migration: spreading through soil and water
senses.titleCN: 污染物迁移：在土壤与水中扩散
senses.definition: the movement of a substance, especially a pollutant, through soil, water or air
senses.definitionCN: 物质、尤指污染物在土壤、水或空气中的移动
senses.example: The study traced the migration of nitrates into the groundwater.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了硝酸盐向地下水的迁移。
senses.why: Here the mover is not a creature but a substance. The word still means a change of place, and the scientific use adds the question of how far and how fast.
senses.whyCN: 这里移动的不是生物，而是物质。词仍指换地方，科学用法则再加上「多远、多快」的问题。

senses.title: Labour migration: workers following demand
senses.titleCN: 劳动力迁移：工人跟着需求走
senses.definition: the movement of workers between regions or countries in search of employment
senses.definitionCN: 工人为寻找就业而在地区或国家之间移动
senses.example: Seasonal labour migration fills the harvest with hands.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性劳动力迁移为收割季节补足了人手。
senses.why: When the reason for moving is work, the word becomes an economic term. The same journey is now explained by wages rather than by home.
senses.whyCN: 当移动的原因是工作时，这个词就成了经济术语。同一趟行程，如今用工资来解释，而不是用家。

senses.title: Any transfer between systems
senses.titleCN: 一般迁移：在一个系统与另一个系统之间转移
senses.definition: a general transfer from one system, category or state to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种系统、类别或状态转移到另一种的统称
senses.example: The migration of files from paper archives to digital ones took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 把档案从纸质迁到数字形式用了一个年代。
senses.why: The general sense is simply 'a move from one container to another'. It keeps the word usable for archives, accounts, populations and species alike.
senses.whyCN: 一般义就是「从一个容器搬到另一个容器」。这使这个词能用于档案、账户、人口与物种。

intro.en: Migration comes from Latin migratio, the noun of migrare 'to move from one place to another'. English borrowed it in the 17th century, at first for the movement of people, and extended it to animals, cells and data in later centuries. The deeper link to a root meaning 'to change' is generally accepted but not certain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migration 出自拉丁语 migratio，即 migrare「从一处移到另一处」的名词。英语在 17 世纪借入，最初指人的迁移，后来几个世纪才扩展到动物、细胞与数据。它与一个意为「改变」的词根有更深联系，这一点一般认为成立，但并非确证。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Data migration and cell migration become standard phrases as computing and cell biology grow.
items.cn: 随着计算技术与细胞生物学的发展，data migration（数据迁移）与 cell migration（细胞迁移）成为固定说法。

items.en: The study of bird migration gives the word its popular natural-history sense.
items.cn: 对鸟类迁徙的研究赋予这个词流行的自然史含义。

items.en: English migration is recorded, naming the movement of people from one country or region to another.
items.cn: 英语 migration 见于记载，指人从一个国家或地区迁往另一个。

items.en: migratio is the noun of migrare; the same verb gives migrate, migrant, immigrate and emigrate.
items.cn: migratio 是 migrare 的名词；同一个动词给出 migrate、migrant、immigrate、emigrate。

items.en: A reconstructed root *mei- 'to change, go' is often proposed behind migrare, though the connection is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: 常有人为 migrare 提出重构词根 *mei-「改变、行走」，但这一联系一般认为成立，而非已证明。

note.en: The first group separates the two prefixed relatives and one false friend; the second compares words for movement that differ in scale or cause.
note.cn: 第一组把两个带前缀的同族词和一个假朋友分开；第二组比较规模或成因不同的移动类词。

entries.definition: the act of leaving one's own country to settle elsewhere. The prefix e- 'out' fixes the point of view at the country of departure.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国到别处定居的行为。前缀 e-「向外」把视角固定在出发国。

entries.definition: the act of coming into a country to settle. The prefix im- 'in' fixes the point of view at the receiving country, so the same journey is emigration or immigration depending on who is counting.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某国定居的行为。前缀 im-「向内」把视角固定在接收国，因此同一趟行程，看谁在计数，就或叫移出或叫移入。

entries.definition: a severe recurring headache. It comes through French from Greek hēmikrania 'half the skull', and has nothing to do with migrare despite the shared opening.
entries.definitionCN: 反复发作的剧烈头痛。它经法语来自希腊语 hēmikrania「半个头骨」，虽开头相同，却与 migrare 无关。

entries.definition: any change of position. It is the widest word, with no implication of settling, season or distance.
entries.definitionCN: 任何位置变化。它是最宽泛的词，不含定居、季节或距离的意味。

entries.definition: the act of moving a person, company or object to a new place. It is usually a single planned move, where migration suggests many moves or a recurring pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 把个人、公司或物件搬到新地点。它通常指一次有计划的搬迁，而 migration 暗示许多次移动或反复出现的模式。

entries.definition: the forcing of people from their homes by war, disaster or development. It stresses that the move was compelled, not chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 因战争、灾害或开发而被迫离开家园。它强调移动是被迫而非自愿。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: migrare means 'to move from one place to another'; every sense is that verb wearing a different subject.
normal.cn: migrare 意为「从一处移到另一处」；每个义项都是这个动词换了个主语。

normal.en: e- 'out' and im- 'in' split the family: emigration looks from the leaving side, immigration from the arriving side.
normal.cn: e-「向外」与 im-「向内」把这个词族分开：emigration 从离开方看，immigration 从到达方看。

normal.en: Migraine is not a relative: its Greek source means 'half the skull', not 'moving away'.
normal.cn: migraine 不是同族词：它的希腊来源意为「半个头骨」，而不是「迁走」。

normal.en: The -tion ending names the event, while migrant names the person who performs it.
normal.cn: -tion 词尾命名事件，而 migrant 命名实施这一行为的人。

normal.en: Data and cells migrate in the same grammatical way as birds: something leaves one place for another.
normal.cn: 数据与细胞的「迁移」在语法上和鸟一样：某物离开一处去另一处。

abstract.en: Picture a dotted line from one marsh to another, followed each year by a new generation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从这片湿地连到那片湿地的虚线，每年由新一代沿着它飞。

abstract.en: Any migration has three parts: a place left, a route, and a place arrived at; every sense uses those three.
abstract.cn: 任何迁移都有三部分：离开的地方、路线、抵达的地方；每个义项都用到这三样。

abstract.en: The word never asks whether the move was good, only that it happened and in which direction.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不过问迁移好不好，只问它是否发生、朝哪个方向。

examples.en: Rural migration has emptied many mountain villages.
examples.cn: 乡村人口外迁让许多山村空了。

examples.en: The migration of monarch butterflies covers thousands of kilometres.
examples.cn: 帝王蝶的迁徙要跨越数千公里。

examples.en: The company scheduled the data migration for a weekend.
examples.cn: 公司把数据迁移安排在周末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买个雷神」——候鸟一路买个雷神当路标，年年迁往同一处 → migration 迁徙、迁移

root: 拉丁语 migrare「从一处移到另一处」→ migratio → 英语 migration。核心是「离开一处、沿路、抵达另一处」，主语可以是人、鸟、细胞、数据或污染物。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a dotted line from one place to another. What changes is who or what travels along it — settlers, birds, whole populations, records, cells, dissolved chemicals, workers, or any transferable thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：从一处连到另一处的一条虚线。变化的只是沿这条线走的是什么——定居者、鸟、整批人口、记录、细胞、溶解的化学物质、工人，或任何可转移之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: at dusk a wedge of birds leaves one marsh for another.
core.cn: 核心意象：暮色中一群鸟排成人字，离开一片湿地飞向另一片。

branches.en: PEOPLE MOVING: settlers change home, and workers change region in search of wages.
branches.cn: 人的移动：定居者换了家，工人为工资换了地区。

branches.en: ANIMALS MOVING: the same route is flown or walked each season, often back and forth.
branches.cn: 动物的移动：同一路线每个季节被飞过或走过，常常来回。

branches.en: THE WAVE: many journeys counted together become a demographic or ecological trend.
branches.cn: 浪潮：许多趟行程合并计数，就成为人口或生态趋势。

branches.en: INVISIBLE MOVERS: records leave one system, cells leave one position, both by the same literal image.
branches.cn: 看不见的移动者：记录离开一套系统，细胞离开一个位置，两者用的是同一个字面意象。

branches.en: SUBSTANCES AND TRANSFERS: pollutants travel through soil and water, and any item can be moved between containers.
branches.cn: 物质与转移：污染物穿过土壤与水，任何东西都可以从一个容器搬到另一个。

intro.en: Migration is Latin migr- plus -ation. The ending -ation names an action; the stem migr- comes from migrare 'to move from one place to another', and the prefixes e- and im- decide the direction of the move.
intro.cn: migration 是拉丁词干 migr- 加 -ation。词尾 -ation 命名动作；词干 migr- 来自 migrare「从一处移到另一处」，而前缀 e- 与 im- 决定移动的方向。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is migrare 'to move, change place'. Its family splits by prefix: e- 'out' gives emigrate, im- 'in' gives immigrate, and trans- 'across' gives transmigrate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 migrare「移动、换地方」。其词族按前缀分流：e-「向外」给出 emigrate，im-「向内」给出 immigrate，trans-「穿过」给出 transmigrate。

items.meaning: the act of moving from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 迁移；迁徙（-ation 构成动作名词）

items.meaning: to move from one region or system to another
items.example: Many birds migrate along this coast.
items.exampleCN: 许多鸟沿着这条海岸迁徙。

items.meaning: a person or animal that migrates
items.exampleCN: 这个营地安置着外来务工人员。

items.meaning: given to migrating, or relating to migration
to leave one's country to settle elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 移出本国；迁往外地（e- 表示向外）
items.exampleCN: 她家在 1980 年代移居国外。

items.meaning: the act of leaving a country
items.example: Emigration drained the island of young workers.
items.exampleCN: 人口外迁让这座岛失去了年轻劳力。

items.meaning: to come into a country to settle
items.meaningCN: 移入；移民入境（im- 表示向内）
items.exampleCN: 他们带着三个孩子移居入境。

items.meaning: the act of entering a country to settle
a passage across, or the passing of a soul into another body
items.meaningCN: 横越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 表示穿过）
items.example: The old doctrine taught the transmigration of souls.
items.exampleCN: 这一古老教义讲灵魂的转世。

items.structure: the same adjective used in medicine for pain that moves
items.meaning: of symptoms that shift from one part to another
items.meaningCN: （医学）游走性的：症状从一处移到另一处
items.example: The patient reported migratory joint pain.
items.exampleCN: 病人诉称有关节游走性疼痛。

latinEntries.meaning: forms a noun of action or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词

definition_zh: 迁徙的；迁移的；游牧的；流动的；季节性的；候鸟的；过路的；游走性的（医学）
definition_en: given to migrating, relating to migration, or moving from one place or part to another rather than staying fixed
core_image: 一条看不见的旧航线被一代代鸟沿着山谷飞过
scene: 这里指「迁徙的」。 The same invisible route over the valley is followed by a new generation every autumn: the birds are migratory.
sceneCN: 这里 migratory 是「迁徙的」（第 1 个义项：动物迁徙的）；句意：每年秋天新一代鸟沿着山谷上空同一条看不见的路线飞行，这些鸟是迁徙的。图中可辨识物件：山谷、飞行的鸟群、虚线航线、秋季的树、远处的湖。

senses.title: Of animals that migrate: moving with the season
senses.titleCN: 动物迁徙的：随季节移动
senses.definition: describing animals that travel from one region to another with the seasons, often returning later
senses.definitionCN: 指随季节从一个地区移到另一地区、且常常之后再返回的动物
senses.example: The wetland is a stopover for migratory birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湿地是候鸟的中途停歇地。
senses.why: Latin migratorius is the adjective of migrare 'to move from place to place'. Applied to animals, it marks a habitual traveller rather than a one-time mover.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 migratorius 是 migrare「从一处移到另一处」的形容词。用在动物身上，它标记的是一种习惯性的旅行者，而不是只搬一次家的人。

senses.title: Of peoples who move with pasture or season
senses.titleCN: 游牧的：随牧草或季节移动的族群
senses.definition: describing human groups that move from place to place rather than settling permanently
senses.definitionCN: 指不永久定居、而在各地之间移动的人群
senses.example: Migratory herders follow the grass up the valley each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 游牧的牧人每年夏天沿着山谷跟着草场往上走。
senses.why: The same adjective extends to people whose way of life is movement. Here it is not a journey but a pattern, so migratory describes a condition rather than an event.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也用于以移动为生活方式的人。这里不是一趟行程，而是一种模式，所以 migratory 描述的是一种状态，而不是一个事件。

senses.title: Of workers who move where work is
senses.definition: describing workers who move from place to place or season to season in search of employment
senses.definitionCN: 指为寻找工作而随地点或季节移动的工人
senses.example: Migratory farm workers arrive for the harvest and leave after it.
senses.exampleCN: 流动的农业工人收割前到来，收完就离开。
senses.why: A migratory worker is not a settler. The adjective signals that residence is temporary and tied to demand, which makes it an economic description.
senses.whyCN: 流动工人不是定居者。这个形容词表明居住是暂时的、随需求而定，因此它是一种经济描述。

senses.title: Seasonal: following a yearly cycle
senses.titleCN: 季节性的：跟着一年一轮的周期
senses.definition: describing movement that follows a yearly cycle rather than a single departure
senses.definitionCN: 指按年度周期进行的移动，而不是一次性的离开
senses.example: The species shows a migratory pattern tied to rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种表现出与降雨相关的迁徙规律。
senses.why: Because migrare can be repeated, the adjective often carries the idea of a cycle. The pattern, not the single trip, is what the word describes here.
senses.whyCN: 因为 migrare 可以反复发生，这个形容词常带周期性。此处它描述的是模式，而不是单趟旅程。

senses.title: migratory birds: the birds themselves
senses.definition: used as a fixed phrase for birds that migrate, especially those protected across borders
senses.definitionCN: 作为固定说法指会迁徙的鸟，尤指受跨境保护的种类
senses.example: Migratory birds are protected by an international treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 候鸟受一项国际条约保护。
senses.why: The phrase migratory birds became a legal and conservation category because such birds cross jurisdictions. The adjective turns a habit into a protected class.
senses.whyCN: migratory birds（候鸟）这一说法成为法律与保育类别，因为这类鸟跨越管辖边界。形容词把一种习性变成了一个受保护的类别。

senses.title: Of behaviour that moves rather than stays
senses.titleCN: 迁移性的：行为本身是移动的
senses.definition: describing behaviour, habits or strategies that involve moving on rather than remaining
senses.definitionCN: 指涉及继续前行而非停留的行为、习性,或策略
senses.example: The study compared migratory and settled strategies among nomads.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较了游牧者的迁移策略与定居策略。
senses.why: Here the adjective modifies an abstract noun. It transfers the animal image to behaviour, so a migratory strategy is one that keeps moving when conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词修饰抽象名词。它把动物的意象转到行为上，因此迁移性策略就是在条件变化时继续移动的策略。

senses.title: Passing through: here for a season only
senses.definition: describing people or animals that stay in a place only briefly while travelling
senses.definitionCN: 指在旅途中只在一地短暂停留的人或动物
senses.example: The town's population doubles with migratory visitors each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天，过路的访客让这个镇的人口翻倍。
senses.why: On the receiving side, a migratory group is one that has not come to stay. The adjective marks temporary presence, which is why host towns plan for it separately.
senses.whyCN: 从接收地看，迁移群体是并不打算留下来的群体。形容词标记的正是这种临时在场，所以东道城镇要为它单独规划。

senses.title: In medicine: symptoms that move about
senses.titleCN: 医学上的游走性：症状到处跑
senses.definition: describing pain or symptoms that shift from one part of the body to another
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛或症状从身体一处转移到另一处
senses.example: Migratory joint pain can be an early sign of some infections.
senses.exampleCN: 游走性关节痛可能是某些感染的早期征象。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the word for what moves within the body instead of between places. The core idea of leaving one location for another survives the change of scale.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个词借来表示在体内移动、而非在地区间移动的东西。「离开一处去另一处」这一核心观念在尺度改变后仍然成立。

intro.en: Migratory comes from Latin migratorius, an adjective of migrare 'to move from one place to another'. English borrowed it in the 18th century, first describing animals and peoples that move with the seasons. The -ory ending marks a tendency or a capacity, like -atory in other Latin adjectives. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migratory 出自拉丁语 migratorius，是 migrare「从一处移到另一处」的形容词。英语在 18 世纪借入，最初描述随季节移动的动物与人群。-ory 词尾标记倾向或能力，如同其他拉丁形容词中的 -atory。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Migratory becomes a legal and conservation term, as treaties protect migratory birds and migratory species across borders.
items.cn: migratory 成为法律与保育术语，条约开始跨境保护候鸟与迁徙物种。

items.en: The adjective spreads to workers and herders, and medicine adopts it for shifting pain.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩展到工人与牧人，医学也采用它来表示游走性疼痛。

items.en: English migratory is recorded, borrowed from Latin migratorius to describe animals and peoples that move with the season.
items.cn: 英语 migratory 见于记载，借自拉丁语 migratorius，描述随季节移动的动物与人群。

items.en: migratorius is formed on migrare 'to move' with the suffix -torius, which marks what tends to do the action.
items.cn: migratorius 由 migrare「移动」加后缀 -torius 构成，后者标记倾向于做该动作的事物。

items.en: The deeper root behind migrare is often reconstructed as *mei- 'to change, go', though the link is generally accepted and not certain.
items.cn: migrare 背后更深的词根常被重构为 *mei-「改变、行走」，但这一联系一般认为成立，并非确证。

note.en: The first group separates the noun relative and one false friend; the second compares adjectives of movement that differ in permanence and cause.
note.cn: 第一组把名词性同族词与一个假朋友分开；第二组比较在持久性与成因上不同的移动类形容词。

entries.definition: a person or animal that migrates, or a worker who moves for work. The noun names the traveller, while migratory describes the travelling habit.
entries.definitionCN: 会迁移的人或动物，或为工作而流动的人。名词指旅行者本身，而 migratory 描述的是这种旅行的习性。

entries.definition: the movement itself, seen as an event. The adjective adds no idea of destination or direction.
entries.definitionCN: 移动本身，被看成一个事件。形容词不添加目的地或方向的信息。

entries.definition: a severe headache. Its Greek source hēmikrania means 'half the skull', so it is not part of the migrare family.
entries.definitionCN: 剧烈的头痛。其希腊来源 hēmikrania 意为「半个头骨」，因此不属于 migrare 词族。

entries.definition: belonging to a way of life with no permanent settlement. It stresses the absence of a home base, while migratory stresses repeated movement.
entries.definitionCN: 属于没有永久定居点的生活方式。它强调没有大本营，而 migratory 强调反复移动。

entries.definition: lasting only a short time, or staying briefly. It focuses on shortness of stay, not on the habit of travelling.
entries.definitionCN: 只持续很短时间，或指短暂停留。它关注停留之短，而非旅行的习性。

entries.definition: happening at a particular season of the year. It names the timing, while migratory names the movement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一年中特定季节发生。它说的是时间，而 migratory 说的是移动本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The -ory ending, as in obligatory or preparatory, marks a tendency, so migratory marks a tendency to move.
normal.cn: -ory 词尾如 obligatory、preparatory 那样标记倾向，所以 migratory 标记「倾向于移动」。

normal.en: migration is the journey, migrant is the traveller, migratory is the habit: one stem, three jobs.
normal.cn: migration 是行程，migrant 是行者，migratory 是习性：一个词干，三个岗位。

normal.en: -atory in Latin adjectives usually points back to a verb, and migrare is that verb.
normal.cn: 拉丁形容词里的 -atory 通常回指某一个动词，而 migrare 就是那个动词。

normal.en: Migraine means 'half the skull' in Greek and only looks like a relative.
normal.cn: migraine 在希腊语里意为「半个头骨」，只是看起来像同族词。

normal.en: The same word covers birds, herders, harvest workers and shifting pain: all of them refuse to stay put.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖鸟、牧人、收割工和游走性疼痛：它们都不肯待在一处。

abstract.en: Picture a dotted route worn into the sky by generations; the route, not the bird, is what repeats.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被一代代鸟磨出的空中虚线；重复的是这条路线，而不是哪一只鸟。

abstract.en: Anything described as migratory treats place as temporary and movement as normal.
abstract.cn: 凡被称作 migratory 的东西，都把地点视为暂时，把移动视为常态。

abstract.en: The word always answers the question: does this stay, or does it come and go?
abstract.cn: 这个词总在回答一个问题：这东西是留下的，还是来来去去的？

examples.en: The delta is critical habitat for migratory waterfowl.
examples.cn: 这片三角洲是迁徙水禽的关键栖息地。

examples.en: Migratory workers follow the strawberry harvest north.
examples.cn: 流动工人跟着草莓收获季一路向北。

examples.en: Some fevers produce a migratory rash.
examples.cn: 有些发热会出现游走性的皮疹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买个雷神托瑞」——买个雷神当向导，一季一迁，从不长住 → migratory 迁徙的、流动的

root: 拉丁语 migrare「从一处移到另一处」＋-torius（表示倾向的形容词后缀）→ migratorius → 英语 migratory。核心是「不肯长住，按季节或按活计反复移动」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a route flown again each season. What changes is who follows it — birds, herders, harvest workers, a yearly pattern, a protected class of birds, a strategy, temporary visitors, or pain moving inside a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：每季又被飞过一次的路线。变化的只是谁沿着它走——鸟、牧人、收割工、年度规律、受保护的一类鸟、一种策略、临时访客，还是体内游走的疼痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one invisible route over a valley, flown by a new generation each autumn.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷上空一条看不见的路线，每年秋天由新一代飞过。

branches.en: THE CYCLE: the tendency to move shows up as seasonal travel that repeats rather than as a single departure.
branches.cn: 周期：移动的倾向表现为反复的季节旅行，而不是一次性的离开。

branches.en: PEOPLE ON THE MOVE: herders follow pasture and workers follow wages; both treat home as temporary.
branches.cn: 流动的人：牧人跟着草场，工人跟着工资；两者都把家当作临时的。

branches.en: THE PROTECTED CLASS: the phrase migratory birds turns a habit into a legal category.
branches.cn: 受保护的类别：migratory birds（候鸟）这一说法把一种习性变成法律类别。

branches.en: THE STRATEGY: behaviour itself can be migratory, moving on when conditions change.
branches.cn: 策略：行为本身也可以是迁移性的，条件一变就继续前行。

branches.en: PASSING THROUGH: visitors stay a season, and in medicine the same word marks pain that shifts place.
branches.cn: 过路：访客只待一季；医学里同一个词标记会换地方的疼痛。

intro.en: Migratory is Latin migrat- plus -ory. The ending -ory, from Latin -torius, marks what tends to do something; the stem is the participle of migrare 'to move from place to place'.
intro.cn: migratory 是拉丁词干 migrat- 加 -ory。词尾 -ory 出自拉丁语 -torius，标记倾向于做某事的事物；词干是 migrare「从一处移到另一处」的分词形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb is migrare with its participle migrat-, and the suffix -torius. Its prefixed relatives e- and im- mark direction of movement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词是 migrare，其分词词干为 migrat-，后缀是 -torius。带前缀的同族词 e- 与 im- 标记移动方向。

definition_zh: 轻微的；不严重的；温和的；和善的；暖和的；（味道）淡的
definition_en: not severe or harsh in degree; gentle and kind in manner; warmer than expected for the season; and soft rather than sharp in taste

scene: 冬日的午后阳光斜照进院子，石阶上一点风也没有，老猫在墙根下慢慢伸了个懒腰。The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
sceneCN: 这里是「天气暖和的、温和的」（第 3 个义项：天气不冷冽）；句意为这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。图中可辨识物件：斜照的阳光、石阶、伸懒腰的猫。

pos.zh: 轻微的；温和的；暖和的；味淡的
