senses.title: Not severe or harsh in degree
senses.definition: not strong, serious or severe, especially of illness, pain or a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 不强烈、不严重、不厉害，尤用于疾病、疼痛或惩罚
senses.example: He had a mild fever and stayed home for one day.
senses.exampleCN: 他发了低烧，在家待了一天。
senses.why: Old English milde meant gentle and merciful, so this sense measures severity by how little force is used rather than by how much there is.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 milde 意为温和、仁慈，所以这一义项是用「用力之少」来衡量严重程度，而不是看它有多少力量。

senses.title: Gentle and kind in character or manner
senses.definition: kind, gentle and not easily angry in the way someone speaks or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行事和气、温和，不轻易发怒
senses.example: Her mild reply quietened the room more than any argument could.
senses.exampleCN: 她温和的回答比任何争辩都更能让房间安静下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense was moral: milde described a person who holds back anger, and that gentleness of character is still the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思带有道德色彩：milde 形容一个人压得住怒气；这种性情上的温和至今仍是这个词的中心。

senses.title: Warmer than expected for the season
senses.definition: used of weather or a climate that is not as cold or as harsh as it could be
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气或气候，表示没有本该有的那么冷、那么严酷
senses.example: The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。
senses.why: Once the word means little force, it fits weather as well, because a mild winter is simply one that uses less of winter's force.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词表示「用力很小」，它也适用于天气：一个温和的冬天，就是冬天没怎么使出它的力气。

senses.title: Not strong in taste or effect
senses.definition: having a soft, not sharp taste, or a gentle effect on the body
senses.definitionCN: 味道柔和、不刺激，或对身体作用平缓
senses.example: The cheese is mild, so it suits people who dislike sharp flavours.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪味道清淡，适合不喜欢刺激口味的人。
senses.why: The same measure of low intensity transfers from pain to the tongue, so a mild cheese is one that hits the mouth with very little force.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「强度低」从疼痛转到舌头上：味道淡的奶酪，就是以很小的力气碰触口腔的那种。

intro.en: Mild goes back to Old English milde meaning gentle and merciful; it belongs to the Germanic branch and has no reliable Latin cognate.
intro.cn: mild 可追溯到古英语 milde，意为温和、仁慈；它属于日耳曼语这一支，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The adjective is generally traced to a Germanic form meaning gentle or kind, though its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个形容词来自日耳曼语中表示「温和、和善」的形式，但其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Milde meant gentle, merciful and kind, and it applied to rulers, judges and ordinary people alike.
items.cn: milde 意为温和、仁慈、和善，可用于君主、法官，也可用于普通人。

items.en: Middle English mild kept the moral sense of gentleness and began to describe weather and taste as well.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mild 保留「性情温和」的道德义，并开始形容天气与味道。

items.en: Writers extended mild from people to seasons, medicines and flavours, wherever force was noticeably low.
items.cn: 文人把 mild 从人扩展到季节、药物与味道，凡是用力明显较小之处都可以用它。

items.en: Modern English uses mild most often for small degrees of illness, gentle manners, soft weather and light flavours.
items.cn: 现代英语中，mild 最常用于轻微的病、和气的举止、温和的天气与清淡的味道。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on mild and one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for gentleness, slightness and softness.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mild 上的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示温和、轻微与柔软的词。

entries.definition: In a gentle way, or only a little.
entries.definitionCN: 以温和的方式，或只稍微地。

entries.definition: The quality of being gentle or not severe.
entries.definitionCN: 温和或不严重的性质。

entries.definition: A fungus that grows on damp surfaces; only the spelling is close and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 生长在潮湿表面的霉；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having a gentle way of behaving, built from mild and mannered.
entries.definitionCN: 举止温和的，由 mild 与 mannered 构成。

entries.definition: Soft and kind in manner, without force.
entries.definitionCN: 举止柔和、善意，不带强势。

entries.definition: Not hard or sharp, either to touch or to hear.
entries.definitionCN: 触感或听感上不硬、不刺。

entries.definition: Small in degree or amount, said of damage or change.
entries.definitionCN: 程度或数量小，用于损伤或变化。

entries.definition: Neither too much nor too little, kept within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 既不过多也不过少，保持在限度之内。

entries.definition: Mild and steady, especially of climate.
entries.definitionCN: 温和而稳定，尤指气候。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on an Old English adjective for gentleness; its family keeps returning to small force, soft weather and the kind of manner that holds anger back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个意为温和的古英语形容词上，同族词反复回到「用力很小」、柔和的天气，以及压得住怒气的举止。

normal.en: Milde in Old English meant gentle and merciful, so mild begins as a moral word rather than a medical one.
normal.cn: 古英语 milde 意为温和、仁慈，所以 mild 起初属于道德词汇，而不是医学词汇。

normal.en: The word measures how little force is used, which is why a mild fever and a mild winter feel like the same idea.
normal.cn: 这个词衡量的是「用力有多小」，所以轻微发烧与温和的冬天感觉上是同一个想法。

normal.en: Milder and mildest add -er and -est, because mild is a short adjective that takes the regular comparison.
normal.cn: milder 与 mildest 分别加 -er 与 -est，因为 mild 是短形容词，走规则比较级。

normal.en: Mildly adds -ly and keeps the meaning of small force or gentle manner.
normal.cn: mildly 加 -ly，保留了「力气小」或「举止温和」的意思。

normal.en: Mildew looks close but means a mould; the two words only share a shape, not a source.
normal.cn: mildew 看上去很像，却指霉菌；两个词只共用外形，不共用来源。

abstract.en: A word for gentleness that also measures illness suggests that kindness and severity sit on one single scale.
abstract.cn: 一个既指温和又能衡量病情的词说明：善意与严重程度坐在同一把尺子上。

abstract.en: Mild weather is winter using less of its force, a picture that makes climate feel almost like a person holding back.
abstract.cn: 温和的天气就是冬天少用了些力气，这个画面让气候几乎像一个人收住了手。

abstract.en: Because mild can describe a voice, a fever and a cheese, the word quietly claims that force is what all three have in common.
abstract.cn: 因为 mild 能形容嗓音、发烧和奶酪，这个词其实在说：三者共通之处就是「力气的大小」。

examples.en: He had a mild fever and stayed home for one day.
examples.cn: 他发了低烧，在家待了一天。

examples.en: The winter here is almost mild enough for the cat to sleep outdoors.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天暖和得几乎能让猫睡在户外。

examples.en: The cheese is mild, so it suits people who dislike sharp flavours.
examples.cn: 这种奶酪味道清淡，适合不喜欢刺激口味的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迈尔德」——迈着慢步、脾气很软的人；记住 mild 是温和的、轻微的。

root: 古英语 milde（温和的、仁慈的）来自日耳曼语中表示「和善」的形式；一般认为其更早来源不确定，且没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is low force; the senses spread from a slight illness to a gentle manner, soft weather and a light taste.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「用力很小」；义项从轻微的病扩到和气的举止、柔和的天气与清淡的味道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a winter afternoon, sunlight falling across a yard, a cat stretching on the stone steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：冬日午后，阳光斜照进院子，一只猫在石阶上伸了个懒腰。

branches.en: a thermometer showing only a small rise
branches.cn: 温度计上只升了一小格

branches.en: a soft answer that ends an argument
branches.cn: 一句结束争吵的柔和回答

branches.en: a cat sleeping outside in midwinter
branches.cn: 隆冬里睡在户外的猫

branches.en: a pale cheese that does not bite the tongue
branches.cn: 一块不刺激舌头的浅色奶酪

branches.en: a nurse speaking softly about a small fever
branches.cn: 护士低声说着轻微的发热

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English adjective of gentleness, its Middle English respelling, and English endings that build the adverb, the noun and the comparative.
intro.cn: 这个词由意为温和的古英语形容词、中古英语拼写，以及构成副词、名词与比较级的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mild: the word belongs to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: mild 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的；军队；军方
definition_en: relating to soldiers, armed forces, or war; also, as a noun, the armed forces of a country taken as one body
core_image: 一队士兵踏着同一节奏行进，枪挎在肩，靴底压过碎石
scene: 天刚亮，一队士兵沿着山口悄悄行进，靴底踩得碎石作响。At dawn the military column moved through the pass without a sound, rifles slung and boots crunching on the gravel.
sceneCN: 这里 military 是「军事的、军队的」（第 1 个义项：属于军队或战争的）；句意：黎明时分，这支军队的队伍悄无声息地穿过山口，枪挎在肩上，靴子踩得碎石作响。场景要点：天刚亮、狭窄山口、成列行进的士兵、肩上的步枪、碎石上传来的靴声；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的
军队；军方（与定冠词连用，the military）

collocations.zh: 军队；军方（作为一个整体）

derivatives.zh: 军国主义；尚武精神
军国主义者；军事迷
军国主义的；黩武的
使军事化；使军队化
军事化
在军事上；以军事手段

senses.title: Of soldiers and war
senses.definition: relating to soldiers, armies, or the conduct of war in general
senses.definitionCN: 与士兵、军队或战争行为有关的
senses.example: The museum's new wing is devoted to military history.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的新展区专门展示军事史。
senses.why: Latin militaris was simply the adjective of miles, 'soldier'. Anything it described belonged to the soldier's world, and that broad belonging is still the first sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 militaris 就是 miles（士兵）的形容词。它修饰的任何东西都属于士兵的世界，这种宽泛的归属至今仍是英语里的第一个义项。

senses.title: Done by soldiers, for soldiers
senses.titleCN: 由军人执行、供军队使用
senses.definition: carried out by soldiers or intended for the armed forces, rather than merely discussing them
senses.definitionCN: 由军人执行或供武装部队使用的，而不只是谈论军队
senses.example: The old airfield is now used for military training.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧机场现在用于军事训练。
senses.why: The adjective does not only label a topic; it also marks who acts and who benefits. A military operation is planned and run by soldiers, so the word moves from 'about soldiers' to 'by and for soldiers'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不只标注话题，还标明谁在行动、谁在受益。军事行动由军人筹划和执行，于是这个词从“关于士兵”走到“由士兵做、为士兵做”。

senses.title: Soldier-like precision
senses.definition: used figuratively of behaviour that is as exact, orderly, and disciplined as a soldier's
senses.definitionCN: 比喻像军人一样精确、整齐、守纪律的行为
senses.example: She folded the map with military precision and handed it back.
senses.exampleCN: 她以军人般的精确折好地图，递了回去。
senses.why: Soldiers drill until every movement is measured and repeated. The adjective borrows that drilled exactness and lends it to civilian actions that have nothing to do with armies.
senses.whyCN: 士兵反复操练，直到每个动作都被量得准确、重复得整齐。这个形容词借来那种操练出来的精确，借给与军队无关的日常动作。

senses.title: By force, not by talk
senses.definition: describing a solution or spirit that relies on armed force or favours it
senses.definitionCN: 形容依靠武力或崇尚武力的解决办法与精神
senses.example: The dispute was settled by military means after talks failed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判失败后，这场争端以军事手段解决。
senses.why: If the soldier's instrument is force, then calling a solution military announces that force will be used. The adjective shifts from describing an institution to recommending its method.
senses.whyCN: 如果士兵的工具是武力，那么把一个解决办法称为军事的，就是在宣告将动用武力。这个形容词从描述一种机构，转为推荐它的手段。

senses.title: The whole body of soldiers
senses.definition: with the definite article, the armed forces of a country considered as one collective body
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，指一国的武装力量整体
senses.example: The military were called in to clear the roads after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，军队被调来清理道路。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by taking 'the': the military, short for the military forces. A collective noun names all the soldiers as one thing, just as the column in the core image moves as one body.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词加上定冠词就变成了名词：“the military”，是“the military forces”的省略。集合名词把所有士兵命名成一个东西，正如核心意象里的队伍作为一个整体移动。

senses.title: The military as a power bloc
senses.titleCN: 军方：作为政治权力机构
senses.definition: the armed forces viewed as an institution that can act in politics and hold power
senses.definitionCN: 把武装部队看作能够在政治中行动、掌握权力的机构
senses.example: The military seized power overnight and closed the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 军方一夜之间夺取政权，并关闭了议会。
senses.why: Once the column of soldiers acts as a single actor in public life, 'the military' stops meaning a crowd of men and starts meaning an institution with its own will and weight.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这支队伍在公共生活中作为一个单一行动者行事，the military 就不再指一群士兵，而开始指一个有自己的意志与分量的机构。

senses.title: One soldier, old-fashioned
senses.definition: in older usage, a soldier or a military man, countable and now rare
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指一名军人或军事人员，可数，现已罕见
senses.example: The old novel describes a retired officer simply as 'a military'.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小说把一名退役军官径称为“一名军人”。
senses.why: The noun first named one person, 'a military man' (1736), before it named the whole body. The singular use survives only as an archaism, a fossil of the earlier step.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词先指一个人，即“a military man”（1736 年），后来才指整个群体。单数用法只作为古语残存下来，是较早那一步的化石。

senses.title: Service in the ranks
senses.definition: in phrases such as 'in the military', the state or career of serving in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在“in the military”一类短语中，指在武装部队中服役的状态或经历
senses.example: He spent six years in the military before returning to the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他服役六年，之后回到农场。
senses.why: To be in the military is to stand inside that collective body. The core image of a formed column becomes a place a person can enter, belong to, and leave.
senses.whyCN: 身处军队，就是站进那个集体之中。核心意象里列队成形的队伍，变成了一个人可以进入、归属并离开的地方。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: used attributively to name an academic field whose subject is armies, wars, and defence
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，命名以军队、战争与防务为对象的学科领域
senses.example: She teaches military history at the war college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在军事学院教授军事史。
senses.why: The same adjective that marks soldiers' business can mark the study of that business. The object of the field is still the column, only now it is observed from a desk instead of a trench.
senses.whyCN: 标记士兵事务的同一个形容词，也可以标记对这一事务的研究。这个领域的对象仍是那支队伍，只是现在是从书桌前观察，而不是从战壕里。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective that English borrowed through French in the fifteenth century; the collective noun arrived three centuries later, and the origin of the Latin base is still unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: military 是 15 世纪经法语借入英语的拉丁语形容词；集合名词要晚三百年才出现，而拉丁语词根的来历至今没有定论。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as militari, 'pertaining to or befitting soldiers; used, done, or brought about by soldiers'. It came from Old French militaire (14c.) and directly from Latin militaris.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 militari，意为“与士兵有关或适合士兵的；由士兵使用、完成或造成的”。它来自古法语 militaire（14 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 militaris。

items.en: Latin militaris meant 'of soldiers or war, of military service, warlike'. It was formed from miles (genitive militis), 'soldier', a word of unknown origin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 militaris 意为“士兵的、战争的、兵役的、尚武的”。它由 miles（属格 militis）“士兵”构成，而这个词的来历不明。

items.en: The origin of miles is unsettled. It may be Etruscan, or it may mean 'one who marches in a troop', which would connect it to Sanskrit melah 'assembly' and Greek homilos 'assembled crowd'. De Vaan finds it tempting to link it to milia 'thousands', hence *mili-it- 'who goes with the thousand'. None of these is proved.
items.cn: miles 的来历没有定论。它可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，也可能意为“随队伍行进的人”，从而与梵语 melah“集会”、希腊语 homilos“聚集的人群”相联系。De Vaan 认为把它与 milia“数千”联系起来很诱人，即 *mili-it-“随千人同行的人”。这些说法都未被证明。

items.en: The noun first meant 'a military man' (1736). 'Soldiers generally' is recorded from 1757, and it is commonly used only with the definite article.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“军人”（1736）。泛指“士兵、军队”的用法记录于 1757 年，而且通常只与定冠词连用。

items.en: The adjective spreads into fixed phrases: military age, the age at which one becomes liable for service (1737); military police (1827); and military-industrial complex, coined in Eisenhower's farewell speech (1961).
items.cn: 这个形容词扩散到固定短语中：military age 指应服兵役的年龄（1737）；military police 即军事警察（1827）；military-industrial complex 即军工复合体，由艾森豪威尔在告别演说中铸成（1961）。

items.en: Militia is a separate borrowing: 1580s, 'system of military discipline', from Latin militia 'military service', and only from the 1690s 'citizen army'. Militarism (1841) came from French militarisme. Military is the adjective, militia the citizen body, militarism the ideology.
items.cn: militia 是另一次借入：16 世纪 80 年代指“军事训练制度”，来自拉丁语 militia“兵役”，到 17 世纪 90 年代才指“公民军队”。militarism（1841）来自法语 militarisme。military 是形容词，militia 是公民武装，militarism 是主义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin miles stem but has drifted into different jobs; the second compares the ordinary words for organized fighters.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语 miles 词干，却各自漂向不同的职责；第二组比较表示有组织武装人员的常用词。

entries.definition: a body of citizens enrolled for military service in an emergency, not professional soldiers. It is a force, while military is the adjective of the professional institution.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急时征召服役的公民队伍，不是职业军人。它是一支力量，而 military 是职业军队的形容词。

entries.definition: willing to use strong or violent action for a cause, or a person who is. It describes a stance or a person, never an army as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意为某项事业采取强硬或暴力行动的，或指这样的人。它描述一种立场或一个人，从不指整支军队。

entries.definition: the belief that a country should keep a strong military and use it aggressively. It names a doctrine, not the forces themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 认为国家应保持强大军力并积极使用武力的信念。它命名一种主义，而不是军队本身。

entries.definition: organized and armed like an army but outside the official armed forces. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the difference from regular military bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 组织与武装像军队、却处于正规武装力量之外的。前缀 para-“在旁”标出它与正规军事组织的区别。

entries.definition: the branch of a country's forces that fights on land, or a large body of soldiers. It is one service, while the military can mean all services together.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量中在陆地作战的分支，或一大群士兵。它是一个军种，而 the military 可指所有军种的整体。

entries.definition: the combined military forces of a country, including army, navy, and air force. It is the full official phrase for what 'the military' names in one word.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量的总和，包括陆军、海军与空军。它是对 the military 一词所指对象的完整正式说法。

entries.definition: soldiers, especially those serving in a particular place or operation. It counts people, while the military names an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 士兵，尤指在某一地点或行动中服役的人。它数的是人，而 the military 命名的是一种机构。

entries.definition: organized groups of soldiers, often qualified as land, air, or naval forces. It is a flexible plural, close to 'the military' but usually needs a qualifier.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的军人群体，常以陆地、空中或海上限定。它是灵活的复数，接近 the military，但通常需要限定语。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, the -ary ending, and the separate but related borrowings militia and militarism.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris、后缀 -ary，以及另行借入但相关的 militia 与 militarism。

normal.en: miles is Latin for 'soldier'; militaris is its adjective. Military begins as nothing more than 'of the soldier'.
normal.cn: miles 是拉丁语的“士兵”，militaris 是它的形容词。military 最初不过是“士兵的”。

normal.en: The adjective came first, in the fifteenth century; the noun 'the military' for soldiers as a body is recorded only in 1757.
normal.cn: 形容词先出现，在 15 世纪；把士兵作为整体来称的 the military 直到 1757 年才有记录。

normal.en: The -ary ending makes an adjective, so military, militarily, militarism and militarize all grow from the same stem with different endings.
normal.cn: -ary 结尾使它成为形容词，所以 military、militarily、militarism、militarize 都从同一词干加上不同词尾长出来。

normal.en: militia is a separate borrowing from Latin militia 'military service'; its 'citizen army' sense is only from the 1690s.
normal.cn: militia 是从拉丁语 militia“兵役”另行借入的词；它的“公民军队”义要到 17 世纪 90 年代才出现。

normal.en: The definite article matters: the military is the whole body, while a military is an old-fashioned way to say one soldier.
normal.cn: 定冠词很关键：the military 指整个军队，而 a military 是旧式说法，指一名军人。

abstract.en: Picture a column of boots striking gravel at the same instant. The sound is not many sounds but one sound repeated, and that is what makes it military.
abstract.cn: 想象一列靴子在同一瞬间踏在碎石上。那声音不是许多声音，而是一个声音的重复，正是这种重复使它成为“军事的”。

abstract.en: The adjective is a uniform that can be put on anything: a bridge, a budget, a history, a way of folding a map.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词是一套可以套在任何东西上的制服：一座桥、一份预算、一段历史、一种折地图的方式。

abstract.en: When the column stops marching and starts deciding, it becomes 'the military' — one actor with a will, not a crowd of men.
abstract.cn: 当这支队伍停止行进、开始作决定，它就变成了“军方”——一个有意愿的行动者，而不是一群士兵。

examples.en: Military spending rose for the third year in a row.
examples.cn: 军费开支连续第三年上升。

examples.en: The airfield is still under military control, and no civilian flights are allowed.
examples.cn: 这座机场仍处于军事管制之下，不允许民用航班起降。

examples.en: After the earthquake, the military was sent in to reopen the mountain roads.
examples.cn: 地震之后，军队被派去重新打通山路。

dict_mnemonic.text: “米里特力”——米里藏着一群特别有力气的壮汉，列队扛枪向前 → military 军事的；军队（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 miles“士兵”的形容词 militaris，核心是“属于士兵与军队的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of military, all growing from one picture: a body of soldiers moving as a single column, and then acting as a single institution.
sensesIntro.cn: military 的九个义项都长自同一幅画面：一队士兵作为一个整体行进，随后作为一个整体机构行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of soldiers stepping as one body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队士兵作为一个整体迈步。

branches.en: SOLDIER'S WORLD: the adjective first marks what belongs to soldiers, then what is done by them and for them.
branches.cn: 士兵的世界：这个形容词先标记属于士兵的东西，再标记由士兵做、为士兵做的事。

branches.en: BORROWED QUALITIES: drilled exactness is lent to civilian actions, and the soldier's instrument, force, is lent to solutions.
branches.cn: 借来的品质：操练出的精确被借给日常动作，士兵的工具即武力被借给解决办法。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND POLITICAL: 'the military' first names all soldiers as one body, then names that body as a power in politics.
branches.cn: 集体与政治：the military 先把所有士兵命名成一个整体，再把这个整体命名为政治中的一种权力。

branches.en: ONE MAN AND A CAREER: the old singular names a single soldier, while 'in the military' names service inside the body.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：旧式单数指一名军人，而 in the military 指在这个整体内部服役。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same adjective marks the academic field that observes armies from a desk.
branches.cn: 研究领域：同一个形容词标记从书桌前观察军队的学科。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective ending in -ary; the stem milit- also carries -ia, -ism, -ist, -istic, -ize and -ation into English. The prefix para- in paramilitary is Greek, added later.
intro.cn: military 是带 -ary 后缀的拉丁语形容词；词干 milit- 还把 -ia、-ism、-ist、-istic、-ize 与 -ation 带进英语。paramilitary 里的前缀 para- 是后来加上的希腊语成分。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words sit behind the family: miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, and militia 'military service'. The origin of miles itself is disputed, so no deeper root can be stated as fact.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族背后有三个拉丁词：miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris，以及 militia“兵役”。miles 本身的来历有争议，因此不能把更深的词根当作事实来陈述。

items.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（milit- 士兵 + -ary 形容词后缀）
items.example: The country keeps a large military budget.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家维持着庞大的军事预算。

items.meaning: in a military way; by military means
items.meaningCN: 在军事上；以军事手段（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The region is militarily important but economically poor.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区军事上重要，经济上却贫穷。

items.meaning: the belief in strong armed forces and their use
items.meaningCN: 军国主义；尚武精神（-ism 构成主义）
items.example: The book traces the rise of militarism before the war.
items.exampleCN: 这本书追溯了战前军国主义的兴起。

items.example: The general was widely seen as a militarist.
items.exampleCN: 这位将军被普遍看作军国主义者。

items.meaningCN: 军国主义的；黩武的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The parade had a strongly militaristic tone.
items.exampleCN: 这场阅兵带有强烈的黩武色彩。

items.meaningCN: 使军事化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The island was militarized during the crisis.
items.exampleCN: 危机期间，这座岛屿被军事化了。

items.meaningCN: 军事化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: People protested against the militarization of the police.
items.exampleCN: 人们抗议警察的军事化。

items.meaning: a citizen army called out in an emergency
items.meaningCN: 民兵组织；紧急时征召的公民武装（拉丁语“兵役”）
items.example: The local militia guarded the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 当地民兵守卫着那座桥。

items.meaningCN: 好战的；激进分子（-ant 构成形容词或指人）
items.example: A militant wing of the movement rejected the talks.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动的激进一派拒绝了谈判。

items.meaning: to work against something, as evidence or circumstance
items.meaningCN: 妨碍；起不利作用（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The high cost militates against any quick repair.
items.exampleCN: 高昂的成本不利于任何快速修复。

items.meaning: armed like an army but outside it
items.meaningCN: 准军事的（para- 在旁 + military 军事的）
items.example: A paramilitary group controlled the border road.
items.exampleCN: 一个准军事组织控制着那条边境公路。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（miles 士兵 + -aris 形容词后缀）
士兵（词源不明，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语）

definition_zh: 矿物；矿物质；（营养）无机盐
definition_en: a naturally occurring inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and structure, and by extension such substances in nutrition
core_image: 一块带晶面的矿石放在木托盘上，旁边一小堆白色晶体盐
scene: 地质课上，老师把一块深色矿石样本传给学生看。The sample was a dark mineral with a metallic lustre, harder than glass.
sceneCN: 这里 mineral 指「矿物」（第 1 个义项：天然产出的无机固体，有确定成分与结构）；它呈深色、带金属光泽，硬度超过玻璃。图中可辨识物件：矿石标本、晶面、木托盘、硬度测试片；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 矿物；矿物质；（复数）无机养分、矿质元素
矿物的；含矿物的（如 mineral water、mineral resources）

derivatives.zh: 使矿化；使变成矿物
矿化；成矿作用
矿物学
矿物学家
矿物学的

senses.title: A natural inorganic solid
senses.titleCN: 矿物：天然产出的无机固体
senses.definition: a naturally formed inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and a characteristic crystal structure
senses.definitionCN: 天然形成的无机固体，具有确定的化学成分与特征晶体结构
senses.example: Quartz is a mineral made of silicon and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 石英是由硅与氧构成的矿物。
senses.why: Geology defines minerals by four tests at once: natural, inorganic, definite composition, ordered structure.
senses.whyCN: 地质学同时用四条标准界定矿物：天然、无机、成分确定、结构有序。

senses.title: Dietary minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿物质养分：人体必需的无机元素
senses.definition: in nutrition, the inorganic elements such as calcium, iron and zinc that the body needs in small amounts
senses.definitionCN: 营养学中指钙、铁、锌等人体少量必需的无机元素
senses.example: Leafy greens supply calcium and other minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 绿叶蔬菜提供钙与其他矿物质。
senses.why: Nutrition borrowed the geology word because these nutrients arrive as mineral salts rather than as carbon compounds.
senses.whyCN: 营养学借用地质学词汇，因为这些养分以矿物盐而非碳化合物的形式到来。

senses.title: Mineral water and springs
senses.titleCN: 矿泉水：含溶解矿物质的天然水
senses.definition: water drawn from a spring and containing dissolved mineral salts, often sold as a drink
senses.definitionCN: 取自泉水、含溶解矿物盐的水，常作为饮品出售
senses.example: The hotel serves local mineral water from the valley spring.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆供应来自山谷泉眼的当地矿泉水。
senses.why: The adjective simply says what the water contains, and the phrase mineral water then became a product category.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是说明水含有什么，而「矿泉水」这一短语随后成了一个产品类别。

senses.title: Mineral resources and rights
senses.titleCN: 矿产资源与矿权：法律经济意义上的矿物
senses.definition: in law and economics, the valuable inorganic substances in the ground and the rights to extract them
senses.definitionCN: 法律与经济中指地下有价值的无机物质及开采它的权利
senses.example: The state owns all mineral rights beneath private land.
senses.exampleCN: 私有土地之下的一切矿权归国家所有。
senses.why: Because extraction is worth money, the word shifts from a scientific category to a legal asset.
senses.whyCN: 由于开采具有经济价值，这个词从科学分类转成了法律资产。

senses.title: Rock-forming minerals
senses.titleCN: 造岩矿物：组成岩石的基本单元
senses.definition: in petrology, the individual mineral species whose grains make up a rock
senses.definitionCN: 岩石学中指构成岩石颗粒的各个矿物种类
senses.example: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩是由石英、长石与云母等矿物构成的岩石。
senses.why: Petrologists must name the parts as well as the whole, so mineral is the countable unit inside an uncountable rock.
senses.whyCN: 岩石学家既要命名整体也要命名部件，因此 mineral 是岩石这个不可数整体中的可数单元。

senses.title: Ore minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿石矿物：值得开采提炼的矿物
senses.definition: the mineral in a deposit that contains a metal or other element valuable enough to extract
senses.definitionCN: 矿床中含金属或其他元素、值得提炼的矿物
senses.example: Chalcopyrite is the main ore mineral of copper.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铜矿是铜的主要矿石矿物。
senses.why: Mining distinguishes the valuable grains from the worthless gangue, so ore mineral is a commercial as well as a geological label.
senses.whyCN: 采矿把有价值的颗粒与无价值的脉石分开，因此矿石矿物既是地质标签也是商业标签。

senses.title: The mineral kingdom
senses.titleCN: 矿物界：旧自然分类中的第三界
senses.definition: in older natural history, the third division of the natural world beside the animal and vegetable kingdoms
senses.definitionCN: 旧自然史中指与动物界、植物界并列的自然界第三界
senses.example: Old textbooks divided nature into animal, vegetable and mineral kingdoms.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书把自然分为动物界、植物界与矿物界。
senses.why: Before modern chemistry, classifying by kingdom was the easiest way to place lifeless matter.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，按「界」分类是把无生命物质归位的最简便方法。

senses.title: Specimens and gems
senses.titleCN: 矿物标本与宝石：收藏与鉴赏对象
senses.definition: a cut or collected mineral specimen valued for colour, crystal form or rarity
senses.definitionCN: 因颜色、晶形或稀有性而被切磨或收藏的矿物标本
senses.example: The museum displays minerals from old copper mines.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出旧铜矿出产的矿物标本。
senses.why: Collectors treat the same scientific object as an aesthetic one, so the word also names what sits in a display case.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者把同一个科学对象当作审美对象，因此这个词也指展柜里的东西。

intro.en: Mineral comes from Medieval Latin minerale, from minera 'ore, mine'. The deeper origin of minera is disputed and may be Celtic.
intro.cn: mineral 出自中世纪拉丁 minerale，源自 minera「矿石、矿」。minera 的更深来源有争议，可能来自凯尔特语。

items.en: Medieval Latin minera meant 'ore, mine, pit'. It appears in mining and metallurgical texts from the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera 意为「矿石、矿、矿坑」，见于中世纪末的采矿与冶金文献。

items.en: Many etymologists link minera to a Celtic root for ore, seen in Welsh mwyn 'ore'. This link is generally accepted but not proved.
items.cn: 许多词源学家把 minera 与表示矿石的凯尔特词根联系起来，可见威尔士语 mwyn「矿石」。这一联系被普遍接受，但未经证实。

items.en: Others derive it from Latin minari 'to jut, to project', because ore bodies stand out from the rock. This explanation is less favoured.
items.cn: 另有人把它追溯到拉丁 minari「突出、伸出」，因为矿体在岩石中显眼。这一解释较少被采纳。

items.en: Old French mineral passed into English in the late Middle Ages, first as an adjective for substances dug from the earth.
items.cn: 古法语 mineral 在中世纪末进入英语，最初作形容词，指从地下挖出的物质。

items.en: Chemistry fixed the modern geological definition in the nineteenth century, and nutrition later borrowed the word for dietary elements.
items.cn: 化学在 19 世纪确立了现代地质学定义，营养学后来又借这个词指膳食元素。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the origin of minera is unresolved; both the Celtic and the Latin minari explanations are hypotheses, and the first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定：minera 的来源尚无定论；凯尔特说与拉丁 minari 说都属假说，英语首见年代亦存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words built on mineral that name studies or processes rather than the substance; the second holds earth materials that are often called minerals loosely.
note.cn: 第一组是由 mineral 构成、却指学科或过程的词；第二组是常被宽泛称作矿物的地球材料。

entries.definition: The scientific study of minerals, their composition, structure and classification. It is a discipline, not a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 研究矿物的成分、结构与分类的学科。它是一门学问，不是物质。

entries.definition: To convert organic matter into mineral form, or to impregnate something with minerals.
entries.definitionCN: 把有机物转化为矿物形态，或用矿物浸染某物。

entries.definition: Describes something that has been converted into or impregnated with mineral matter, such as mineralized bone.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被转化为矿物或被矿物浸染的事物，如矿化骨。

entries.definition: A natural aggregate of one or more minerals. A rock is the whole mixture; a mineral is one ingredient.
entries.definitionCN: 由一种或多种矿物组成的天然集合体。岩石是整体混合物，矿物是其中一种成分。

entries.definition: A solid whose atoms are arranged in a repeating pattern. Many minerals form crystals, but glass is a solid without that order.
entries.definitionCN: 原子呈重复排列的固体。许多矿物形成晶体，但玻璃是缺乏这种有序性的固体。

entries.definition: Rock or mineral material rich enough in a metal to be mined at a profit. All ore contains minerals, but most minerals are not ore.
entries.definitionCN: 金属含量高到值得开采获利的岩石或矿物材料。矿石都含矿物，但多数矿物并非矿石。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: minera 'ore' + -ale: what comes out of a mine.
normal.cn: minera「矿石」+ -ale：从矿里出来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs mineralize, mineralization, mineralogy, mineralogist and mineralogical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mineralize、mineralization、mineralogy、mineralogist、mineralogical。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: mineral water, mineral resources, mineral deposit, essential minerals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：矿泉水、矿产资源、矿床、必需矿物质。

normal.en: A rock is a mixture; a mineral is one ingredient with a fixed formula.
normal.cn: 岩石是混合物；矿物是成分固定的一种配料。

normal.en: Nutrition calls calcium and iron minerals because they arrive as inorganic salts.
normal.cn: 营养学把钙与铁称为矿物质，因为它们以无机盐形式到来。

abstract.en: Picture a cut stone with flat shiny faces lying on a wooden tray.
abstract.cn: 想象一块切开的石头，平面闪亮，躺在木托盘上。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of still water with a faint mineral taste and a spring behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯静水，带一点矿物味，背后是一眼泉。

abstract.en: Picture an old chart dividing the world into animal, vegetable and mineral bands.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧图把世界分成动物、植物与矿物三条带。

examples.en: The region is rich in mineral deposits but short of water.
examples.cn: 该地区矿产丰富，却缺水。

examples.en: Iron is a mineral that many people do not get enough of.
examples.cn: 铁是许多人摄入不足的一种矿物质。

examples.en: The geologist identified the green mineral as malachite.
examples.cn: 地质学家把那块绿色矿物鉴定为孔雀石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mine（矿）+ ral」——从矿里挖出来的东西 → mineral 矿物

root: 中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石、矿」→ minerale → 古法语 mineral → 英语 mineral。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one substance from a crystal in rock to a nutrient in food, a product on a shelf, a legal right, an ore, an old kingdom and a museum specimen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种物质从岩石中的晶体走到食物里的养分、货架上的产品、法律上的权利、矿石、旧时的「界」与博物馆标本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faceted stone on a tray beside a heap of white salt crystals.
core.cn: 核心意象：木托盘上的晶面矿石，旁边一小堆白色盐晶。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: the definition needs nature, no life, a fixed formula and an ordered structure.
branches.cn: 地质：定义需要天然、无生命、成分固定与结构有序四条。

branches.en: NUTRITION: the same word names the inorganic elements the body needs.
branches.cn: 营养：同一个词指身体所需的无机元素。

branches.en: PRODUCT: dissolved salts turn spring water into a branded drink.
branches.cn: 产品：溶解的盐把泉水变成有品牌的饮品。

branches.en: VALUE: rights underground and ore in the vein both measure the word in money.
branches.cn: 价值：地下的权利与矿脉中的矿石，都用钱来衡量这个词。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION AND BEAUTY: an old kingdom and a display case are two ends of the same label.
branches.cn: 分类与美：旧时的「界」与展柜，是同一标签的两端。

intro.en: Mineral is a Medieval Latin noun ending in -ale, the suffix that turns a stem into a thing name, later used as an adjective without change.
intro.cn: mineral 是带 -ale 的中世纪拉丁名词，该后缀把词干变成事物名，后来它又原形用作形容词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin minera supplied the stem and minerale the noun; the -alis ending later produced English mineralogy through a different path.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera 提供词干、minerale 提供名词；-alis 词尾后来经另一条路径产生了英语 mineralogy。

items.meaning: a natural inorganic solid; also an adjective
items.meaningCN: 天然无机固体；也作形容词
items.example: The mineral is harder than steel.
Soil microbes mineralize the organic matter.
items.exampleCN: 土壤微生物把有机质矿化。
矿化作用保存了这具化石。
矿物学按对称性给晶体分类。
矿物学家鉴定了这块标本。

items.example: The mineralogical survey mapped the district.
items.exampleCN: 矿物学调查绘制了该区地图。

items.meaning: to remove minerals from water or bone
items.meaningCN: 从水或骨中去除矿物质
items.example: The filter demineralizes the tap water.
items.exampleCN: 该过滤器去除自来水中的矿物质。

items.meaning: a person who works in a mine
items.example: The miners went down at dawn.

latinEntries.structure: minera, minerae (f., Medieval Latin, first declension)

latinEntries.meaning: a thing dug from the earth

definition_zh: 最小的；极少的；最低限度的；极简风格的
definition_en: the smallest or least possible in amount, size or degree
core_image: 一只几乎见底的杯子，杯壁上只剩一道水痕
scene: 舞台上一张桌子、两把椅子，再无他物，灯光只照向演员。The set is minimal, with one table and two chairs on an empty stage.
sceneCN: 这里指布景精简到最低限度（第 3 个义项：去掉装饰、只留必要的样式）；句意为布景极简，空舞台上只有一桌两椅。

pos.zh: 最小的；极少的；最低限度的；极简的

derivatives.zh: 最低限度地；极简地
极简主义；极简风格
极简主义者；极简的
极简风格的

senses.title: The smallest possible amount
senses.definition: the least amount or degree that is possible in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某种情形下可能达到的最小数量或程度
senses.example: The plan was changed at minimal cost to the company.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划以对公司最低的成本做了改动。
senses.why: The Latin superlative minimus already fixes the word at the bottom of a scale, so the sense is the floor rather than merely something small.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语最高级 minimus 已把词固定在刻度最底端，因此这一义项指下限，而不只是尺寸小。

senses.title: The lowest acceptable level
senses.definition: the lowest level that still meets a requirement
senses.definitionCN: 仍然满足要求的最低水平
senses.example: The committee set minimal standards for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为安全设定了最低标准。
senses.why: Once a standard exists, the word marks the line below which a thing no longer counts.
senses.whyCN: 标准一旦存在，这个词就标出低于它便不算数的那条线。

senses.title: A stripped-down style
senses.definition: a style that removes decoration and keeps only what is necessary
senses.definitionCN: 去掉装饰、只保留必要元素的风格
senses.example: The poster uses minimal type and a single image.
senses.exampleCN: 这张海报只用极少的字体和一张图。
senses.why: Design borrowed the word to name the beauty of leaving things out.
senses.whyCN: 设计借这个词来命名「删到不能再删」的美。

senses.title: Barely noticeable in degree
senses.definition: so slight that it is hard to notice
senses.definitionCN: 轻微到几乎难以察觉
senses.example: The two versions differ by a minimal amount.
senses.exampleCN: 两个版本之间只有极小的差别。
senses.why: At this end of the scale the word approaches zero without reaching it.
senses.whyCN: 在这一端，这个词逼近零却没有到零。

senses.title: A smallest element in mathematics
senses.definition: an element or set than which nothing smaller satisfies the conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在给定条件下没有更小者能满足的元或集合
senses.example: The proof rests on a minimal set of assumptions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依赖一组极小的假设。
senses.why: Logic needs a name for the floor of a chain, and the Latin superlative supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学需要给链的底端一个名字，拉丁语最高级正好提供。

senses.title: A minimal pair in linguistics
senses.definition: two words that differ in one sound and therefore in meaning
senses.definitionCN: 只差一个音、因而意义不同的两个词
senses.example: Cat and bat form a minimal pair in English.
senses.exampleCN: 「猫」与「球棒」的英文词只差一个音，构成一组最小对立对。
senses.why: The term marks the smallest sound difference that still changes meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语标出仍能改变意义的最小语音差别。

senses.title: The least intrusive option
senses.definition: the choice that disturbs people or systems least
senses.definitionCN: 对人或系统打扰最小的选择
senses.example: Engineers chose the minimal intervention that fixed the fault.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师选择了能排障的最小干预。
senses.why: In repair and policy the word means doing as little as possible.
senses.whyCN: 在维修与政策中，这个词表示尽量少动手。

senses.title: Reduced art or music
senses.definition: art or music built from very few repeated elements
senses.definitionCN: 只用很少几个反复元素构成的艺术或音乐
senses.example: The minimal piece holds one chord for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这首极简作品让同一个和弦持续了好几分钟。
senses.why: The 1960s movements took the word as a banner for reduction itself.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪六十年代的流派把这个词当作「减法」的旗帜。

intro.en: Minimal joins the Latin superlative minimus, meaning smallest, to the English adjective suffix -al. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: minimal 把意为「最小」的拉丁语最高级 minimus 与英语形容词后缀 -al 结合。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代是约数。

items.en: Minimus is the superlative of parvus, small, and means the smallest member of a group.
items.cn: Minimus 是 parvus「小的」的最高级，意为一组中最小者。

items.en: Medieval music named its shortest note value with the same superlative, and English kept minim for a half note.
items.cn: 中世纪音乐用同一个最高级命名最短的音符时值，英语保留 minim 指二分音符。

items.en: Learned French used minimal for the least or smallest before English borrowed the adjective.
items.cn: 学术法语先用 minimal 表示「最小」，英语随后借入。

items.en: Minimal appears in English in the nineteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: minimal 在十九世纪进入英语，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century design and art attached the word to forms stripped to essentials.
items.cn: 二十世纪的设计与艺术把这个词系到删到只剩必要的形式上。

items.en: Mathematics, linguistics and policy all use it for the floor of a scale.
items.cn: 数学、语言学与政策领域都用它指一个刻度的下限。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin small-root family; the second group names ideas close to the least end of a scale.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「小」的词族；第二组是接近刻度最低端的近义说法。

entries.definition: To reduce something to the least possible amount; built on minimum rather than on minimal.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物减到最少；由 minimum 而非 minimal 构成。

entries.definition: The lowest point or amount that is allowed or recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 被允许或记录的最低点、最低量。

entries.definition: A half note in older music, named with the same Latin superlative.
entries.definitionCN: 旧记谱法中的二分音符，用同一个拉丁最高级命名。

entries.definition: Smaller or less important; a Latin comparative from the same small-root family, not a form of minimal.
entries.definitionCN: 更小的、次要的；同属「小」词族的拉丁比较级，不是 minimal 的变形。

entries.definition: Less; the sign for subtraction, from the same comparative stem.
entries.definitionCN: 较少；减号，来自同一比较级词干。

entries.definition: The smallest amount in a group or scale.
entries.definitionCN: 一组或一个刻度中数量最小的。

entries.definition: Small in degree and often barely worth noticing.
entries.definitionCN: 程度小，常指几乎不值得注意。

entries.definition: So small that it can be disregarded.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以忽略不计。

entries.definition: Barely enough, often with a hint of shortage.
entries.definitionCN: 勉强够，常含不足之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin superlative, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁最高级、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Minimus is the superlative of parvus, so the word starts at the very bottom of small.
normal.cn: minimus 是 parvus 的最高级，因此这个词从「小」的最底端起步。

normal.en: A minimal pair is a pair like cat and bat: one sound apart, two different words.
normal.cn: 最小对立对如「猫」与「球棒」这两个英文词：只差一个音，就是两个词。

normal.en: Minimalism is the art of taking things away until only the necessary remains.
normal.cn: 极简主义就是一路拿掉，直到只剩必要之物。

normal.en: Minimum is the allowed floor, while minimal describes what sits at that floor.
normal.cn: minimum 是允许的下限，minimal 则描述处于该下限的东西。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: minimal cost, minimal impact and minimal change.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：最低成本、最小影响与最小改动。

abstract.en: Minimal is a room with one chair, and the empty space is part of the design.
abstract.cn: 极简是一间只放一把椅子的屋子，空出来的地方也是设计的一部分。

abstract.en: At the bottom of a scale, nothing can be taken away without breaking the thing.
abstract.cn: 在刻度的底端，再拿走任何一点，事物就会散架。

abstract.en: A minimal answer trusts the question to carry what is left unsaid.
abstract.cn: 极简的回答相信问题本身能承担未说出的部分。

examples.en: The report was written in minimal prose, with no decorative clauses.
examples.cn: 这份报告用极简的文笔写成，没有装饰性的从句。

examples.en: A minimal dose was enough to keep the pain away.
examples.cn: 最小剂量就足以止住疼痛。

examples.en: The two designs differ in minimal ways, yet the cost gap is large.
examples.cn: 两个设计差别极小，成本差距却很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迷你猫」——小到只剩一只猫的影子：最小的、极简的

root: 拉丁语最高级 minimus「最小的」← 原级 parvus「小的」；同族比较级 minor「更小的」与 minus「较少」并非由 minimal 派生。英语在十九世纪加上 -al 构成形容词，确切首见年代不确定；minim 另有中世纪音乐「二分音符」之义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all sit at the bottom of a scale: the least amount, the lowest acceptable line, a stripped style, a barely visible degree, a smallest element, a contrastive pair, the least intrusive choice, and reduced art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都落在刻度的底端：最小数量、可接受的最低线、删繁的样式、几乎看不见的程度、极小的元素、最小对立对、最不打扰的选择，以及极简的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup almost empty, one trace of water left on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只几乎见底的杯子，杯壁上只剩一道水痕。

branches.en: THE LEAST: the bottom of any scale of amount.
branches.cn: 最少：任何数量刻度的底端。

branches.en: THE LINE AND THE LIGHT TOUCH: the lowest acceptable standard and the least intrusive act.
branches.cn: 线与轻触：可接受的最低标准，以及打扰最小的动作。

branches.en: THE STRIPPED FORM: design and art that remove until only the essential remains.
branches.cn: 删繁的形式：设计与艺术一路删到只剩必要。

branches.en: THE FAINT DEGREE: a difference that is barely there.
branches.cn: 轻微的程度：几乎不存在的差别。

branches.en: THE SMALLEST UNIT: the floor of a mathematical chain and the one-sound pair of linguistics.
branches.cn: 最小单位：数学链的底端与语言学中只差一音的一对。

intro.en: Minimal is the Latin superlative minimus plus the English suffix -al; the Latin family is clear, and no native root is involved.
intro.cn: minimal 是拉丁语最高级 minimus 加英语后缀 -al；拉丁词族清楚，不涉及本族语词根。

latinIntro.en: Minimus, minor and minus belong to one small-root family, while parvus supplies the plain positive degree.
latinIntro.cn: minimus、minor 与 minus 同属一个表示「小」的词族，parvus 则提供平常的原级。

items.example: The superlative fixes the floor of the scale.
items.exampleCN: 最高级把刻度固定在最底端。

items.example: Parvus supplies the plain positive that minimus replaces.
items.exampleCN: 原级 parvus 提供平常的「小」，由 minimus 承担最高级。

items.example: Minor is the comparative partner, not a form built from minimal.
items.exampleCN: minor 是同级搭档，不是由 minimal 造出的形式。

items.example: The same family gives the word behind the subtraction sign.
items.exampleCN: 同一词族也给出减号背后的说法。

items.example: The noun names the allowed floor and is the base of minimize.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指允许的下限，也是 minimize 的基词。

items.example: English builds the adjective directly on the Latin superlative.
items.exampleCN: 英语直接把这个形容词建在拉丁最高级上。

items.example: The suffix turns the Latin stem into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把拉丁词干变成英语形容词。

items.example: The adverb marks the bottom of a scale of effort.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出用力程度的最低端。

items.meaning: art or design reduced to essentials
items.example: The movement turned the adjective into a banner.
items.exampleCN: 该流派把这个形容词变成旗帜。

items.meaning: two words differing in one sound
items.example: Linguistics names the smallest contrastive unit a pair.
items.exampleCN: 语言学把最小的对立单位称为一对。

definition_en: the smallest amount, level or point that is possible, allowed or reached, or the lowest value of a set or function
core_image: 量筒底部划着一道红线，任何水位都不能低于它
scene: 清晨的水库边，管理员看着水位尺上那道浅浅的红线，提醒同伴抽水不能低于这里。The reservoir is kept at a minimum during the dry months.
sceneCN: 这里 minimum 是「最低水位、最低限度」（第 1 个义项：可能或允许的最小量）；句意为干旱月份水库水位被维持在最低限度。画面里可抓住的物件：水位尺、红线、抽水泵。

pos.zh: 最小值；最低限度；最低点；极小值
最小的；最低的

由 minim- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使减到最少」
由 minimize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「最小化」

senses.title: The smallest possible amount
senses.definition: the smallest amount of something that is possible, needed or allowed
senses.definitionCN: 某事物可能、需要或被允许的最小数量
senses.example: Keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
senses.exampleCN: 十点以后把噪音降到最低。
senses.why: Latin minimum is the neuter form of minimus, the smallest, and it entered English as a noun for the least quantity that can be reached or permitted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minimum 是 minimus（最小的）的中性形式，进入英语时就是一个名词，指能够达到或被允许的最小数量。

senses.title: The lowest point reached
senses.definition: the lowest level or point that a changing quantity falls to before it rises again
senses.definitionCN: 某个变化中的量在下落之后、回升之前所到的最低水平或位置
senses.example: The river reaches its minimum in late summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在夏末降到最低水位。
senses.why: Anything that rises and falls traces a curve, and the bottom of that curve is naturally called its minimum; the word moves from an allowed limit to an observed low.
senses.whyCN: 凡是有起伏的东西都会画出曲线，曲线的最低处自然被叫作 minimum；词义于是从「被允许的下限」转到「观察到的低点」。

senses.title: Lowest allowed by a rule
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean the smallest or lowest that a rule, price or standard permits
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指规则、价格或标准所允许的最小或最低值
senses.example: The minimum age for driving is eighteen in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 许多国家的驾车最低年龄是十八岁。
senses.why: English turns the noun into a modifier by placing it before another noun; minimum wage is the wage at the bottom of the permitted scale, with no ending added.
senses.whyCN: 英语把名词放到另一个名词前面就使它成为修饰语；minimum wage 就是允许范围最底端的工资，词形不加任何词尾。

senses.title: The lowest value of a set or function
senses.definition: the smallest value that a set of numbers or a mathematical function takes
senses.definitionCN: 一组数值或一个数学函数所能取到的最小值
senses.example: The curve has a minimum at the centre and rises on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这条曲线在中央有极小值，两侧向上升高。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a precise name for the bottom of a graph, and it borrowed the Latin word unchanged; the everyday sense of a lower bound became a technical term.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要给图像的最低处一个精确的名字，于是原封不动地借用了这个拉丁词；日常的「下界」义由此变成了术语。

intro.en: Minimum came straight from Latin, where it was the neuter form of the word for smallest; English borrowed it in the seventeenth century as a noun for the least amount.
intro.cn: minimum 直接来自拉丁语，是「最小的」一词的中性形式；英语在十七世纪把它借来，作名词指最小量。

items.en: Parvus meant small; its comparative minor and superlative minimus are generally treated as suppletive forms, borrowed from a related root rather than built with a regular ending.
items.cn: parvus 意为「小的」；一般认为它的比较级 minor 与最高级 minimus 属于补充式形式，借自相关词根，而不是用规则词尾构成。

items.en: Minimus meant the smallest or least, and it supplied the top of the scale in phrases such as minimus natu, the youngest.
items.cn: minimus 意为最小的、最少的；在 minimus natu（最年幼者）这类说法里，它标出等级序列的最末端。

items.en: The neuter singular minimum was used as a noun for the smallest amount, and this exact form was taken over by English.
items.cn: 中性单数形式 minimum 被当作名词使用，指最小量；英语原样借用的正是这个形式。

items.en: Writers borrowed minimum in the seventeenth century, first in scientific and mathematical writing where a precise lower bound was needed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作者借入 minimum，最早用在科学与数学写作中，因为那里需要一个精确的下界。

items.en: Modern English uses it as a noun and as a modifier, and keeps the Latin plural minima beside the English minimums.
items.cn: 现代英语让它作名词也作修饰语，并在英语复数 minimums 之外保留拉丁式复数 minima。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the Latin comparison of small; the near-meaning group collects other words for the least amount or the bottom of a scale.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「小」的比较之上的形式；近义组收其他表示最小量或标度底端的词。

entries.definition: As small as possible; barely enough to count.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能小的；刚刚够得上数的。

entries.definition: To reduce something to the smallest possible amount or level.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物减到尽可能小的数量或程度。

entries.definition: Smaller, less important, or not yet legally adult; it belongs to the same Latin comparison of small.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的、较次要的，或尚未成年的；它属于同一个拉丁「小」的比较系列。

entries.definition: A tiny amount, or a short note value in early music.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的量，或早期音乐中短小的音符时值。

entries.definition: The smallest amount or degree of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物最小的数量或程度。

entries.definition: The lowest level that prices or amounts are allowed to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 价格或数量被允许降到的最低水平。

entries.definition: The lowest point of something, especially of a changing situation.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的最低点，尤指变化中的境况。

entries.definition: The lowest part or level of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的最下部或最低水平。

normalIntro.en: Minimum is the superlative of a Latin word for small, and its family keeps circling the idea of the least amount or the bottom of a scale.
normalIntro.cn: minimum 是拉丁语「小」一词的最高级形式，它的一族词始终围着「最小量」或「标度底端」打转。

normal.en: Minimus is Latin for smallest, and minimum is its neuter form, so the word already carries the comparison inside it.
normal.cn: minimus 是拉丁语「最小的」，minimum 是它的中性形式，所以这个词本身就带着比较。

normal.en: The min- root recurs in minor, minus and minute: all of them measure something smaller or less.
normal.cn: min- 这个词根反复出现在 minor、minus 与 minute 里：它们都在度量更小或更少的东西。

normal.en: Keep something to a minimum is the everyday frame: whatever follows is the thing you want as small as possible.
normal.cn: keep something to a minimum 是日常框架：后面接的东西，就是你希望尽量压小的对象。

normal.en: Minimum wage and minimum age show the word acting as a modifier without any added ending.
normal.cn: minimum wage 与 minimum age 展示了这个词不靠任何词尾就充当修饰语。

normal.en: Maximum is its opposite, built with the Latin superlative for great, so the pair mark the two ends of a scale.
normal.cn: maximum 是它的反面，用拉丁语表示「大」的最高级构成；这一对词标出一段标度的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a red line near the floor of a measuring tube: everything must stay above it.
abstract.cn: 想象量筒底部附近有一道红线，所有东西都必须停在它上面。

abstract.en: A minimum is not zero; it is the lowest point that still counts as acceptable.
abstract.cn: minimum 并不是零，而是仍然算得上合格的最低点。

abstract.en: Every curve that dips has a floor, and English uses one Latin word for that floor.
abstract.cn: 每条下探的曲线都有一个底，英语用一个拉丁词来指这个底。

examples.en: Keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
examples.cn: 十点以后把噪音降到最低。

examples.en: The river reaches its minimum in late summer.
examples.cn: 这条河在夏末降到最低水位。

examples.en: The minimum age for driving is eighteen in many countries.
examples.cn: 许多国家的驾车最低年龄是十八岁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你闷」——空间小得人一进去就发闷，小到不能再小；minimum 是最小值、最低限度。

root: 拉丁语 minimus（最小的）是 parvus（小）的最高级形式；中性形式 minimum 被英语原样借作名词「最小量」。一般认为 minimus 与 minus（较少）、minuere（减少）同属一个词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the least amount; the senses run from an allowed lower limit to an observed low, then to attributive and mathematical uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最小量；各义项从被允许的下限，走到观察到的低点，再延伸到定语用法与数学术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line near the bottom of a measuring tube, marking the lowest level allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：量筒底部附近的一道红线，标出允许的最低水位。

branches.en: a red line that the water must not drop below
branches.cn: 水位不得低于的那道红线

branches.en: a river shrinking to its shallowest week
branches.cn: 河水缩到最浅的那一周

branches.en: a sign at the gate stating the youngest age allowed
branches.cn: 门口写明最低年龄的牌子

branches.en: a curve dipping to a single low point
branches.cn: 曲线下探到唯一的最低点

branches.en: a rulebook with its floor printed in bold
branches.cn: 把下限印得又粗又醒目的规章

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin superlative for small, and its family spreads across adjectives, verbs and nouns about making things less.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「小」的最高级构成，它的一族词散落在形容词、动词与名词里，都与「使之更少」有关。

latinIntro.en: Minimum is the neuter form of the Latin superlative for small, and the same root runs through minor, minus and minimize.
latinIntro.cn: minimum 是拉丁语「最小」最高级的中性形式，同一词根贯穿 minor、minus 与 minimize。

senses.title: A head of a government department
senses.definition: a senior politician who is in charge of a government department
senses.definitionCN: 主管某一个政府部门的资深政界人物
senses.example: The finance minister resigned after the budget vote.
senses.exampleCN: 预算表决之后，财政部长辞职了。
senses.why: Latin minister first meant a servant or attendant; a person who served the crown at the head of an office grew into the modern sense of a senior state official.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minister 最初指仆人、随从；在朝廷里替君主办事、主管一个衙门的人，逐渐长成现代「政府部长」的意思。

senses.title: A religious leader of a congregation
senses.definition: a person ordained to lead worship and care for a congregation, especially in Protestant churches
senses.definitionCN: 受按立以主持礼拜、照看会众的人，尤指新教教会的牧师
senses.example: The minister read the names of the dead aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师大声念出逝者的名字。
senses.why: The same word for a servant was used in the church for one who serves the congregation; the religious sense is older in English than the political one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「仆人」的词在教会里指服侍会众的人；在英语里，宗教义比政治义出现得更早。

senses.title: A diplomat below an ambassador
senses.definition: a diplomatic representative of a country, ranking below an ambassador and above lower embassy staff
senses.definitionCN: 一国派出的外交代表，地位低于大使、高于使馆较低级别的职员
senses.example: She was posted to the embassy as minister for trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她被派往使馆担任贸易公使。
senses.why: Diplomacy borrowed the ranking vocabulary of courts: a minister served a sovereign abroad, and the title stayed for envoys who rank just under an ambassador.
senses.whyCN: 外交沿用宫廷的等级词汇：minister 曾在国外替君主办事，这个头衔便留给地位略低于大使的使节。

intro.en: Minister goes back to a Latin word for a servant, and its journey from household attendant to cabinet member and clergy explains why one word covers three jobs.
intro.cn: minister 可追到拉丁语中表示仆人的词；它从家仆走到内阁成员与神职人员，这条路径解释了一个词为何能涵盖三种职务。

items.en: Minus meant less, and from it Latin built words for people or things that stood lower in a hierarchy.
items.cn: minus 意为较少、较低；拉丁语由它造出表示在等级中位置较低的人或事物的词。

items.en: Minister named an attendant, a servant or an agent who acted for someone else, including an assistant in religious rites.
items.cn: minister 指随从、仆人或替别人办事的代理人，也包括宗教仪式中的助手。

items.en: The verb ministrare meant to serve, to attend or to manage, and it produced a whole family of English words such as administer.
items.cn: 动词 ministrare 意为服侍、随侍或经办，由此产生 administer 等一整族英语词。

items.en: Old French took the noun as menistre, a servant or an official, and carried it into English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 menistre，指仆人或官员，诺曼征服之后传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps minister for a cabinet member, a clergyperson and a mid-ranked diplomat, while ministry splits off as the office itself.
items.cn: 现代英语用 minister 指内阁成员、神职人员与中等层级的外交官，而 ministry 则分出去指职务机构本身。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin stem of service; the near-meaning group collects other titles for officials, clergy and envoys.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「服务」词干上的词；近义组收官员、神职人员与使节的其他称谓。

entries.definitionCN: 与部长、政府部门或牧师职责有关的。

entries.definition: The act of serving or helping, often in a religious setting.
entries.definitionCN: 服侍、帮助的行为，常用于宗教场合。

entries.definition: A senior government official who heads a department in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 美国联邦政府中主管一个部门的资深官员。

entries.definition: A minister in charge of a church and its congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 主管一间教堂及其会众的牧师。

entries.definitionCN: 被派往代表一国的外交官，通常地位低于大使。

entries.definition: A person who holds a position of authority in a government or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 在政府或机构中担任有权威职位的人。

normalIntro.en: The word began as Latin for a servant, and every modern sense still keeps a trace of someone acting on another's behalf.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是拉丁语中的「仆人」，每个现代义项都还留着「替别人办事」的痕迹。

normal.en: Latin minister meant servant or attendant, which is why the word fits both a cabinet member serving the state and a pastor serving a congregation.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 minister 意为仆人或随从，所以这个词既适合替国家办事的内阁成员，也适合服侍会众的牧师。

normal.en: Ministrare is the verb behind administer, so minister and administer are siblings rather than unrelated words.
normal.cn: ministrare 是 administer 背后的动词，所以 minister 与 administer 是同胞词，而非互不相干的词。

normal.en: Ministry is the office, minister is the person: the -y ending names the institution, the bare word names the human being.
normal.cn: ministry 是机构，minister 是人：-y 词尾命名制度，光秃秃的词干则指具体的人。

normal.en: Prime minister is a fixed phrase, and the stress falls on the first word, so it sounds like one title rather than two.
normal.cn: prime minister 是固定说法，重音落在第一个词上，所以听起来像一个头衔而不是两个词。

normal.en: The diplomatic rank is the oldest of the three modern uses in court language, because an envoy was literally a servant sent abroad.
normal.cn: 三个现代义项里，外交级别在宫廷用语中出现得最早，因为使节字面上就是被派往国外的仆人。

abstract.en: Picture a servant holding a sealed letter at a palace door: the same figure becomes a cabinet member and a pastor.
abstract.cn: 想象一个仆人站在宫门口，手里拿着一封封好的信：同一个人物后来变成了内阁成员与牧师。

abstract.en: A minister never acts alone; the word always points to someone who works for another party.
abstract.cn: minister 从不单独行动；这个词始终指向替另一方办事的人。

abstract.en: One Latin noun for service splits into a person, an office and a rank, like a single trunk with three branches.
abstract.cn: 一个表示服务的拉丁名词分成一个人、一个机构与一个级别，像一根主干长出三根枝条。

senses.title: A government department
senses.definition: a department of government led by a minister and responsible for one area of public life
senses.definitionCN: 由部长领导、负责某一方面公共事务的政府部门
senses.example: The Ministry of Health issued new guidance on masks.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部发布了关于口罩的新指引。
senses.why: Latin ministerium meant service or office; when a minister took charge of an area of public service, the office itself came to be called a ministry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ministerium 意为「服务、职务」；当部长主管某一方面的公共事务时，那个职务机构本身就被称为 ministry。

senses.title: The government or its term in office
senses.definition: a government led by a prime minister, or the period during which it holds power
senses.definitionCN: 由总理或首相领导的一届政府，或它掌权的时期
senses.example: The ministry fell after losing a vote of confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁在失去信任投票后倒台。
senses.why: Because a ministry is the whole set of ministers serving together, the word shifted from one department to the cabinet and to the time it stays in power.
senses.whyCN: 因为 ministry 也指共同任职的一整批部长，词义便从一个部门转到整个内阁，再转到它掌权的时期。

senses.title: The office of a religious minister
senses.definition: the profession or work of an ordained religious minister, or the clergy as a body
senses.definitionCN: 受按立牧师的职业与工作，或作为整体的神职人员
senses.example: She left teaching to enter the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开教职，进入神职。
senses.why: The same Latin word for service was applied to the church, where ministry names the work of serving a congregation rather than a government office.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「服务」的拉丁词也被用到教会，这里的 ministry 指服侍会众的工作，而不是政府机关。

intro.en: Ministry is the office built on the Latin noun for service, and English uses it for both a government department and the work of the church.
intro.cn: ministry 是建立在拉丁语「服务」名词之上的职务，英语用它兼指政府部门与教会工作。

items.en: Minister meant a servant or attendant, and everything built on it keeps the idea of service.
items.cn: minister 指仆人或随从，凡由它构成的词都保留了「服务」的观念。

items.en: Ministerium named service, office or function, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: ministerium 指服务、职务或职能，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the word as menistere, meaning office or service, before it passed into English.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 menistere，意为职务或服务，随后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English ministry covered service and the work of the clergy, and the political sense joined it later.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ministry 覆盖服务与神职工作，政治义后来才加入。

items.en: Modern English uses ministry for a department of state, for a whole government, and for the religious vocation.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ministry 指国家部门、整个内阁，以及宗教使命。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of service and management; the near-meaning group collects names for departments, cabinets and clergy.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「服务、管理」词干上的词；近义组收部门、内阁与神职人员的名称。

normal.en: Ministry is built on minister, the person; the -y ending turns the servant into the office he or she holds.
normal.cn: ministry 建立在 minister 这个「人」之上；-y 词尾把仆人变成他所担任的职务。

normal.en: Latin ministerium meant service or function, so ministry is literally the job rather than the building.

normal.en: Ministry of Education, foreign ministry and ministry of defence all show the word naming a branch of government.

normal.en: Administration and administer share the same ministrare root, so the whole family is about handling affairs for someone else.
